docs.title: EpidBot Documentation
docs.text: EpidBot is an AI-powered assistant for analyzing Brazilian and international public health data. It provides a natural language interface to download, query, analyze, and visualize health data from DATASUS, WHO, the World Bank, the Malaria Atlas Project, and many other sources.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Natural Language Interface: Ask questions about health data in English, Portuguese, or Spanish
  • Multi-language UI: Full interface in Portuguese, English, Spanish, Chinese, and Arabic
  • Data Download: Automatically download data from PySUS (SINAN, SIM, SIH, and more)
  • User Datasets: Upload your own CSV, Excel, GeoJSON, and Shapefile data for private analysis
  • SQL Queries: Execute DuckDB SQL queries on parquet files
  • Visualizations: Generate charts, maps, plots, diagrams, and raster visualizations
  • Plot Gallery: Browse, upload, search, and preview all your plots in one place
  • International Data: WHO, World Bank, ECDC, Mosqlimate, PAHO, Malaria Atlas Project, Pathoplexus
  • Knowledge Base: Store and retrieve documentation with vector embeddings
  • Session Management: Maintain conversation history across multiple sessions, with sharing support
  • Report Generation: Create formatted PDF reports with embedded visualizations, version history, and sharing
  • Secure Sandbox: Execute Python code and SQL in an isolated Docker container
  • Onboarding Tutorial: New users receive a guided tour automatically
  • Mid-stream Messaging: Send messages during streaming to interrupt and redirect
  • Voice Input: Speak your queries using browser-based speech recognition
  • Message Editing: Edit and resubmit your last message
  • Chat Export: Export conversations as PDF, Markdown, JSON, HTML, or plain text
  • Message Feedback: Rate assistant responses with thumbs up/down
  • QGIS Plugin: Chat with EpidBot inside QGIS, with map context injection and results loaded back as layers
  • REST API: Full programmatic access via JWT/API key authentication (120+ endpoints)
  • WebSocket Streaming: Real-time streaming chat with tool progress indicators

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  NGINX (reverse proxy, SSL termination)                  │
├─────────────────┬───────────────────┤
│  /              │  /api/            │
│  Next.js :3000  │  FastAPI :8123    │
│  (primary UI)   │  (REST + WS API)  │
└─────────────────┴─────────┬─────────┘
                           │
              ┌────────────┼────────────────┐
              │  PostgreSQL (:5432)         │
              │  DuckDB catalog             │
              │  Parquet files (/data/pysus)│
              │  Sandbox container (:8080)  │
              └─────────────────────────────┘

EpidBot is built with:

  • Next.js — Primary web frontend (React, Tailwind CSS, next-intl)
  • FastAPI — REST API with WebSocket streaming support
  • Pydantic-AI — Agent framework for LLM interactions (50+ tools)
  • PostgreSQL — User accounts, sessions, messages, API keys
  • PySUS — Brazilian health data downloader
  • DuckDB — In-memory SQL engine for querying parquet files
  • Docker — Containerized deployment with sandbox isolation

docs.title: Release Notes
docs.text: Highlights from recent EpidBot releases. For the full change history see the repository commits.

docs.title: Academic Discount: Self-Service Claims with Admin Review
docs.text:
Users who don't have a verified email on an academic domain can now claim the 50% academic discount directly from Settings > Plan:

  • The claim requires a verified email address and records academic_status='requested' — a pending state that never unlocks the discount by itself and is never overwritten by automatic academic-email validation
  • Every active admin is emailed the claimant's profile details (institution, location, ORCID, Google Scholar, plan, member-since) with a link to the admin panel; email failures never break the claim
  • Admins grant or revoke via the new graduation-cap button in the users table (or PUT /admin/users/{id}/academic). Granting emails the user so the review has a visible outcome; revocation stays silent
  • Discount semantics are unchanged: the 50% academic discount still beats (never stacks with) the 30% annual-commitment discount, and is applied automatically at checkout

docs.title: Admin Override: Plans That Never Expire
docs.text:
The admin users table now has a "never expires" checkbox in the Plan column:

  • While set, the plan ignores plan_expires_at entirely — no downgrade by the subscription-expiry job, no grace-period semantics in quota or feature gating
  • Rejected on Free plans (nothing to pin); automatically cleared when a user is downgraded to free or a payment is refunded, so a revoked plan can't stay pinned
  • API: PATCH /admin/users/{id}/plan/never-expires with {"never_expires": true|false}

docs.title: Fixed: API-Key Chats Failing with UnboundLocalError
docs.text: Bare API-key chats (POST /api/v1/chat with an X-API-Key) failed with "cannot access local variable 'ModelRequest'". A conditional in-function import made ModelRequest function-local but unbound whenever no profile/style/document context was attached — which is exactly the API-key path. The import is now unconditional at the top of both the sync and streaming chat paths, with regression tests guarding against reintroduction.

docs.title: Admin MCP Server for External Agents
docs.text:
EpidBot now ships a Model Context Protocol server that lets an external agent query the administrative subsystem and execute admin actions — designing marketing campaigns, creating ads, sending emails, refreshing user profiles — from any MCP-capable client.

  • Streamable-HTTP endpoint at /api/v1/mcp, opt-in via mcp.enabled in config.yaml
  • Dedicated mk_ admin keys (scope='admin_mcp') with the owner's admin role re-checked on every request — demoting an admin revokes MCP access instantly
  • 24 tools: read-only analytics plus campaign/ad/email actions; real-email actions require an explicit confirm=true
  • Every mutation is written to a new admin_audit_log table (actor, key, action, target, result)
  • DNS-rebinding protection on by default — production must list its domain in mcp.allowed_hosts

👉 Full guide: Admin MCP Server

docs.title: User Country Inference in the Admin Panel
docs.text:
The Country column in the admin users table now shows the best available localization estimate per user instead of only the (mostly empty) self-reported profile field:

  1. Confirmed — the user-entered profile country (high confidence)
  2. Chat — a country inferred by the LLM profiling pipeline from chat history (institutions, cities, municipalities), stored in a separate country_llm column so user data stays sacred
  3. Email — the country-code TLD of the email domain (@fiocruz.br → Brazil, .ac.uk → UK; free-mail providers ignored)
  4. Language — the UI language, only for unambiguous locales (pt-BR, zh-CN)

The table renders a colored provenance dot with a tooltip, and the "top countries" stats chart aggregates with the same rules. Backfill by running Admin → Profiles → update (or wait for the scheduled profile cycle).

docs.title: Edge TTS: Free Neural Voices by Default
docs.text:
The default text-to-speech engine is now Microsoft Edge neural voices (edge-tts) — free, no API key. Voice selection is language-aware: the server detects the message language and picks a matching neural voice from a curated catalog covering all interface languages (pt-BR, English, Spanish, Chinese, Arabic).

  • OpenAI and local Piper engines remain one-click fallbacks in the admin panel
  • Gift (group-invite) accounts included; STT/dictation is unchanged

docs.title: Group Invites: Plans Now Revert on Time
docs.text:
Fixed a bug where accounts created through admin group invites kept their gifted plan past the expected date:

  • The invited plan duration is now stored per invite (plan_duration_days, default 30) instead of a hardcoded interval, and the admin form exposes it explicitly
  • Gifted plans no longer receive the 7-day grace period — they revert to free exactly at expiry (paid subscriptions keep the grace window, since real payments deserve the benefit of the doubt)
  • If the user subscribes themselves, renewal works normally and grace applies again

docs.text:

  • Per-invite plan duration badge and form field in the admin UI (all 5 UI languages)
  • Email-country badges and tooltips in the admin users table (5 languages)
  • admin_audit_log table for traceability of MCP-triggered actions
  • New endpoints: POST /payments/academic-claim, GET /payments/discount-status, PUT /admin/users/{id}/academic, PATCH /admin/users/{id}/plan/never-expires
  • Admin UI (all 5 UI languages): academic-discount grant/revoke action and never-expire checkbox in the users table; academic-claim button and under-review badge in Settings > Plan

docs.title: September 2026
docs.text:
• Group invites with gifted subscriptions: admins can create invite links (in the Groups tab) that add redeemers to a group and gift a chosen plan (Pro/Max/Team) — with a configurable link validity, usage cap and now a configurable plan duration
  • Subscription expiry automation: expired paid plans downgrade to free automatically after a grace period, with a notification email

docs.title: Admin MCP Server
docs.text:
EpidBot exposes its administrative subsystem to external agents (Claude Code, Cursor, custom orchestrators, etc.) through a Model Context Protocol server. The agent can query analytics — users, plans, token usage, feature adoption, campaign metrics — and execute admin actions: designing email marketing campaigns, creating in-app ads, sending emails, refreshing user profiles, and more.

The server is opt-in (disabled by default), authenticated with dedicated admin API keys, and every mutating action is written to an audit log.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Transport MCP streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC + SSE) Endpoint /api/v1/mcp (works with or without a trailing slash) Auth X-API-Key: mk_… header (or Authorization: Bearer mk_…) Protocol version MCP 2025-06-18 (via the official mcp SDK) Default state Disabled — enable with mcp.enabled: true in config.yaml Tool surface 24 tools: 14 read-only, 10 actions (no deletes by design) Implementation epidbot/mcp/ — FastMCP + Starlette, mounted by create_app()

Tools reuse the FastAPI route handlers directly, so validation, plan-guard and lifecycle rules (e.g. campaigns are only editable in draft) behave identically to the REST API and the web UI.

External agent ──MCP (streamable HTTP)──► NGINX (/api/) ──► FastAPI :8123
                                                │
                                       /api/v1/mcp
                                                │
                                    ┌───────────┴───────────┐
                                    │  auth middleware      │  mk_ key + live admin role
                                    │  FastMCP (24 tools)   │  → route handlers / services
                                    │  audit writer         │  → admin_audit_log
                                    └───────────────────────┘

docs.title: Enabling the Server
docs.text:
Add an mcp: section to config.yaml and restart the API:

mcp:
  enabled: true
  path: /api/v1/mcp                # mount path (default)
  server_name: epidbot-admin       # name advertised in the MCP handshake
  dns_rebinding_protection: true   # Host/Origin checks (recommended)
  allowed_hosts:                   # Host headers to accept — REQUIRED in production
    - kwar-ai.com.br
    - localhost
    - 127.0.0.1

Production: set mcp.allowed_hosts

The MCP SDK ships with DNS-rebinding protection that rejects any request whose Host header is not in allowed_hosts (HTTP 421). NGINX forwards the real public domain, so production deployments must list it — otherwise every request fails with 421 Misdirected Request. The defaults only allow localhost / 127.0.0.1 (for local development with the MCP Inspector).

Disabling (mcp.enabled: false, the default) skips the mount entirely; the rest of EpidBot is unaffected.

docs.title: API Keys (mk_)
docs.text:
MCP access uses keys that are separate from regular ek_ API keys:

  • Stored in the api_keys table with scope = 'admin_mcp'
  • Prefix mk_ + 64 hex chars; the raw key is shown once at creation
  • The owner must be an admin — and the admin role is re-checked against the database on every request: demoting an admin revokes their MCP access instantly, without touching the key
  • Regular ek_ keys are rejected by the MCP server, and mk_ keys do not work on regular REST endpoints — the two are separate trust domains

docs.title: Managing Keys (admin REST endpoints)
docs.text:
Authenticate with an admin JWT (same as the web admin panel):

# Issue a key (copy the value from the response — it is not retrievable later)
curl -X POST https://your-host/api/v1/admin/mcp-keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_JWT" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "growth-agent"}'
# → {"id": 3, "name": "growth-agent", "key": "mk_9f2c..."}

# List keys (metadata only)
curl https://your-host/api/v1/admin/mcp-keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_JWT"

# Revoke
curl -X DELETE https://your-host/api/v1/admin/mcp-keys/3 \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_JWT"

Duplicate names are rejected (400). Revocation takes effect on the agent's next request.

docs.title: Connecting an Agent
docs.text:
Point the MCP client at https://your-host/api/v1/mcp with the key header. For example, in a Python agent using the official SDK:

from mcp import ClientSession
from mcp.client.streamable_http import streamablehttp_client

async def main():
    async with streamablehttp_client(
        "https://your-host/api/v1/mcp",
        headers={"X-API-Key": "mk_9f2c..."},
    ) as (read, write, _):
        async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
            await session.initialize()
            tools = await session.list_tools()
            result = await session.call_tool("get_user_stats", {})
            print(result.content[0].text)

Desktop clients (Claude Desktop, Cursor, …) use the equivalent JSON configuration:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "epidbot-admin": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://your-host/api/v1/mcp",
      "headers": { "X-API-Key": "mk_9f2c..." }
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Security Model
docs.text:
• Authentication: every request — including initialize and tools/list — passes through the auth middleware; there is no anonymous capability discovery.
  • Authorization: scope='admin_mcp' and live users.role = 'admin' on the key's owner.
  • Confirmation gate: tools that reach real users — send_campaign, send_user_message — refuse to run unless called with confirm=true. The refusal is explicit and audited, so an agent must consciously decide to send.
  • No deletes: the tool surface deliberately excludes delete operations (users, ads, campaigns, templates, groups). Deactivation (is_active=false) is available where it exists; real deletes stay in the web admin panel.
  • Audit trail: every mutating tool call writes a row to the admin_audit_log table — actor, key, action, target, parameters, and outcome (ok / refused / error).
SELECT created_at, actor_username, key_prefix, action, target_type, target_id, result
FROM admin_audit_log
ORDER BY created_at DESC
LIMIT 50;

docs.text: All tools return JSON (serialised pydantic models / dicts). Errors surface as MCP error results with the originating HTTP status, e.g. HTTP 404: Campaign not found.

docs.title: send_campaign 🔒 confirm
docs.text:
Starts sending a draft campaign to its audience as a background job.

Parameter Type Description campaign_id int Must be in draft confirm bool Must be true — real emails go to real users

Returns a job_id for get_job_status. Per-recipient tracking (open pixel, click redirect, unsubscribe link) and language-variant template selection behave exactly like a send from the web panel.

docs.title: send_user_message 🔒 confirm
docs.text:
Sends a direct email to one user through the standard EpidBot email frame.

Parameter Type Description user_id int Recipient subject str Max 200 chars body str Plain text (max 10 000 chars), rendered with white-space preserved confirm bool Must be true

docs.title: refresh_user_profile
docs.text:
Rebuilds one user's profile (interests, usage totals, chat-derived country, …) from their recent sessions.

Parameter Type Default user_id int — use_llm bool true — set false for counts only

Safe by design: user-entered profile fields are never overwritten by automatic updates.

docs.title: refresh_all_profiles
docs.text: Same semantics as the scheduled profile cycle, for all users active in the last 7 days.

docs.title: Typical Workflow: Designing a Campaign
docs.text:
1. get_user_stats()                        → who is on the platform
2. preview_campaign_audience(plans=["free"], languages=["pt-BR"])
                                           → reach estimate + sample
3. create_email_template(...)              → draft copy
4. preview_email_template(template_id)     → review rendering
5. create_campaign(name, template_id, audience)
6. update_campaign(...)                    → iterate while in draft
7. send_campaign(campaign_id, confirm=true)
                                           → returns job_id
8. get_job_status(job_id)                  → poll until completed
9. get_campaign_metrics(campaign_id)       → opens, clicks, revenue

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Cause Fix 401 Invalid, revoked, or non-admin MCP key Key revoked, wrong value, or owner demoted Re-issue the key; check the owner still has role='admin' 401 Missing API key Client not sending the header Configure X-API-Key: mk_… on the client 421 Misdirected Request Host header not in mcp.allowed_hosts Add the public domain to mcp.allowed_hosts and restart Refused: send_campaign(...) was NOT executed Confirmation gate Re-invoke with confirm=true after reviewing the audience HTTP 400: Cannot send campaign with status 'sending' Lifecycle guard Only draft campaigns can be sent; poll until the current job finishes Job status 404 Job expired Jobs are kept for 1 hour after completion Tools listed but calls hang Session manager not running Ensure the app was started through its normal lifespan (systemd/docker), not a bare Starlette app

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
• No delete operations and no user/plan management tools — those stay in the web admin panel (extend deliberately if needed).
  • Background jobs expire after 1 hour; campaign metrics are permanent, but get_job_status for a finished send is not.
  • The endpoint requires a client that supports the streamable-HTTP transport (any MCP client from mid-2025 onwards).

docs.title: Initialize and Scan
docs.text:
import epidbot.catalog as catalog

# Initialize catalog
result = catalog.init_catalog("~/pysus")
print(result)

# Scan for new files
result = catalog.scan_all_parquet_files()
print(result)

docs.title: Query Catalog
docs.text:
# Get summary
summary = catalog.get_catalog_summary()
print(summary)

# Search for specific data
results = catalog.search_catalog("dengue")
print(results)

# Get dataset details
info = catalog.get_dataset_info("dengue_2023")
print(info)

# Get column samples
samples = catalog.get_column_samples("dengue_2023", "UF", limit=10)
print(samples)

docs.title: Manage Path
docs.text:
# Set custom path
catalog.set_data_dir("/data/health-data")

# Get catalog path
path = catalog.get_catalog_path()
print(f"Catalog at: {path}")

docs.title: REST API
docs.text: The EpidBot REST API allows external client software to interact with the EpidBot chat interface programmatically. The API is built with FastAPI and runs on port 8123 (configurable via API_PORT).

docs.title: Base URL
docs.text: http://localhost:8123/api/v1

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text: Interactive API documentation is available at: - Swagger UI: http://localhost:8123/docs - ReDoc: http://localhost:8123/redoc - OpenAPI JSON: http://localhost:8123/openapi.json

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: The API supports two authentication methods:

docs.title: JWT Tokens
docs.text:
1. Register: POST /auth/register
  2. Login: POST /auth/login → returns access_token and refresh_token
  3. Refresh: POST /auth/refresh → use refresh token to get new access token

docs.title: API Keys
docs.text:
1. Create API key: POST /auth/api-keys
  2. Use API key: pass X-API-Key header or api_key query parameter

docs.title: Enabling API Access
docs.text:
Users must have is_api_enabled = true to use the API. Administrators can enable this via: - PUT /admin/users/{user_id}/api-access - Admin panel in the Next.js frontend

MCP access for external agents

External agents can also consume EpidBot administratively over the Model Context Protocol using dedicated mk_ admin keys. See the Admin MCP Server guide for setup, security model and the full tool reference.

docs.text: Endpoint Limit POST /auth/login 10 requests/minute POST /auth/register 5 requests/minute Other endpoints 60 requests/minute

docs.title: POST /chat
docs.text:
Submit a chat message for async processing. Returns a job_id immediately — poll GET /chat/{job_id} for the result. This avoids timeout issues since LLM responses can take 5-120 seconds.

Headers: - Authorization: Bearer <token> or X-API-Key: <key>

Request: 

{
  "message": "Show me dengue cases in São Paulo for 2023",
  "session_id": null,
  "locale": "en"
}

Response (200) — job submitted: 

{
  "job_id": "job_a1b2c3d4e5f6...",
  "session_id": 1,
  "status": "processing"
}

docs.title: GET /chat/{job_id}
docs.text:
Poll for the status and result of a chat job. Recommended polling interval: 2-5 seconds.

Headers: - Authorization: Bearer <token> or X-API-Key: <key>

Response — still processing: 

{
  "job_id": "job_a1b2c3d4e5f6...",
  "status": "processing",
  "created_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:05Z"
}

Response — completed: 

{
  "job_id": "job_a1b2c3d4e5f6...",
  "status": "completed",
  "session_id": 1,
  "content": "Based on the data...",
  "images": ["![plot](plots/abc.png)"],
  "thinking": "The user wants epidemiological data...",
  "created_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:45Z"
}

Response — failed: 

{
  "job_id": "job_a1b2c3d4e5f6...",
  "status": "failed",
  "error": "Error message description",
  "created_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updated_at": "2024-01-01T00:00:10Z"
}

Usage example (curl): 

# Submit
JOB=$(curl -s -X POST https://api.epidbot.kwar-ai.com.br/api/v1/chat \
  -H "X-API-Key: ek_your_key" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message": "teste", "locale": "pt"}')

JOB_ID=$(echo $JOB | jq -r '.job_id')

# Poll until completed
while true; do
  RESULT=$(curl -s https://api.epidbot.kwar-ai.com.br/api/v1/chat/$JOB_ID \
    -H "X-API-Key: ek_your_key")
  STATUS=$(echo $RESULT | jq -r '.status')
  if [ "$STATUS" != "pending" ] && [ "$STATUS" != "processing" ]; then
    echo $RESULT | jq .
    break
  fi
  sleep 3
done

docs.title: WS /chat/stream
docs.text:
WebSocket endpoint for streaming chat responses.

Connection URL: 

ws://localhost:8123/api/v1/chat/stream?token=<jwt>
or 
ws://localhost:8123/api/v1/chat/stream?api_key=<key>

Client → Server Messages:

// Start chat
{"type": "start", "payload": {"message": "...", "session_id": null, "locale": "en"}}

// Cancel ongoing chat
{"type": "cancel"}

// Keep connection alive
{"type": "ping"}

// Poll for job result (if tool started a job)
{"type": "poll", "payload": {"job_id": "..."}}

Server → Client Messages:

// AI is thinking
{"type": "thinking", "data": {"content": "..."}}

// Tool execution started
{"type": "tool_start", "data": {"tool_name": "download_sinan_data", "tool_display": "Download SINAN Data", "code_preview": "...", "timeout": 240}}

// Tool execution completed
{"type": "tool_complete", "data": {"tool_name": "download_sinan_data", "elapsed": 12.5, "has_error": false}}

// Streaming response chunk
{"type": "chunk", "data": {"content": "..."}}

// Final response
{"type": "complete", "data": {"content": "...", "images": [], "usage": {...}}}

// Turn was interrupted by a new user message
{"type": "turn_interrupted", "data": {"partial_content": "..."}}

// Error occurred
{"type": "error", "data": {"error": "..."}}

// Pong response to ping
{"type": "pong"}

// Chat was cancelled
{"type": "cancelled"}

// Heartbeat with optional download progress
{"type": "heartbeat", "data": {"download_progress": 0.5}}

// Job started (async)
{"type": "job_started", "data": {"job_id": "...", "status": "processing"}}

// Job result
{"type": "job_result", "data": {"job_id": "...", "status": "completed", "result": "..."}}

// Tool timed out
{"type": "tool_timeout", "data": {"tool_name": "...", "message": "..."}}

docs.title: 1. Clone and Configure
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/your-org/epidbot.git
cd epidbot

docs.title: 2. Create .env File
docs.text:
cat > .env << 'EOF'
# API Keys (at least one required)
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-key-here

# Security (generate with: python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))")
SECRET_KEY=your-secret-key-here

# Default Admin Credentials
EPIDBOT_ADMIN_USER=admin
EPIDBOT_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change_this_password
EPIDBOT_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@example.com
EOF

docs.title: 3. Start EpidBot
docs.text: docker-compose up -d

docs.title: 4. Get Admin Credentials
docs.text: docker exec epidbot cat /data/.admin_credentials

docs.title: 5. Access Application
docs.text:
Open browser to: http://localhost:3000

Login with the credentials from step 4.

docs.title: 6. Change Password (Important!)
docs.text: docker exec -it epidbot uv run python auth_cli.py passwd admin

docs.title: Required
docs.text: Variable Description Example EPIDBOT_ADMIN_PASSWORD Initial admin password (min 8 chars) SecurePass123! SECRET_KEY Session encryption key Generate with secrets.token_hex(32)

docs.title: Docker User Management
docs.text: This guide explains how to manage users when deploying EpidBot in Docker containers.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
When running EpidBot in Docker, user management works differently than in local deployments. This guide covers:

  1. Automatic Admin Creation: Default admin user created on first run
  2. Creating Additional Users: Using docker exec
  3. Managing Existing Users: Password changes, listing users
  4. Docker Compose Configuration: Setting up environment variables

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: On first startup, EpidBot automatically checks if any users exist in the database. If no users are found, it creates a default admin user using environment variables.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Add these environment variables to your docker-compose.yml:

services:
  epidbot:
    environment:
      - EPIDBOT_ADMIN_USER=admin
      - EPIDBOT_ADMIN_PASSWORD=your-secure-password
      - EPIDBOT_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@example.com

Or in your .env file:

EPIDBOT_ADMIN_USER=admin
EPIDBOT_ADMIN_PASSWORD=your-secure-password
EPIDBOT_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@example.com

docs.title: Security Requirements
docs.text:
• EPIDBOT_ADMIN_PASSWORD is required (no default)
  • Password must be at least 8 characters long
  • Change the default password immediately after first login

docs.title: First Run Behavior
docs.text:
When the container starts for the first time:

Initializing EpidBot...
INFO: Creating default admin user 'admin'...
✓ Default admin user created successfully!
  User ID: 1
  Username: admin
  Email: admin@example.com
  Credentials saved to: /data/.admin_credentials

==================================================
DEFAULT ADMIN CREDENTIALS:
  Username: admin
  Password: your-secure-password
==================================================
IMPORTANT: Change this password immediately!
==================================================

A credentials file is saved to /data/.admin_credentials for reference.

docs.title: Method 1: Using docker exec (Interactive)
docs.text:
Create users interactively:

docker exec -it epidbot uv run python auth_cli.py create-admin

Follow the prompts to create a new user.

docs.title: Method 2: Using docker exec (Non-Interactive)
docs.text:
For automation, use heredoc:

docker exec -i epidbot uv run python auth_cli.py create-admin << EOF
researcher
secure_password_123
secure_password_123
researcher@institute.org
EOF

docs.title: Method 3: Using a Script
docs.text:
Create a script create_user.sh:

#!/bin/bash
docker exec -i epidbot uv run python auth_cli.py create-admin << EOF
$1
$2
$2
$3
EOF

Make it executable and use:

chmod +x create_user.sh
./create_user.sh researcher password123 researcher@example.com

docs.title: List All Users
docs.text:
docker exec -it epidbot uv run python auth_cli.py list

Output:

=== User List ===

ID    Username             Email                          Created              Last Login          
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1     admin                admin@example.com              2026-03-10           2026-03-10          
2     researcher           researcher@institute.org       2026-03-11           Never               

Total: 2 user(s)

docs.title: Change Password
docs.text:
docker exec -it epidbot uv run python auth_cli.py passwd <username>

Example:

docker exec -it epidbot uv run python auth_cli.py passwd researcher

docs.title: Delete User
docs.text:
docker exec -it epidbot uv run python auth_cli.py delete <username>

Example:

docker exec -it epidbot uv run python auth_cli.py delete researcher

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
version: '3.8'

services:
  epidbot:
    build:
      context: .
      dockerfile: Dockerfile
    image: epidbot:latest
    container_name: epidbot
    ports:
      - '3000:3000'
    volumes:
      - 'epidbot_data:/data'
    environment:
      # API Keys
      - 'OPENAI_API_KEY=${OPENAI_API_KEY}'
      - 'ZHIPU_API_KEY=${ZHIPU_API_KEY}'
      - 'DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=${DEEPSEEK_API_KEY}'
      - 'GOOGLE_API_KEY=${GOOGLE_API_KEY}'

      # Service URLs
      - 'LIBBY_URL=http://libby-api:8000'
      - 'OLLAMA_HOST=http://libby-ollama:11434'

      # Session Security
      - 'SECRET_KEY=${SECRET_KEY}'

      # Default Admin User
      - 'EPIDBOT_ADMIN_USER=${EPIDBOT_ADMIN_USER:-admin}'
      - 'EPIDBOT_ADMIN_PASSWORD=${EPIDBOT_ADMIN_PASSWORD}'
      - 'EPIDBOT_ADMIN_EMAIL=${EPIDBOT_ADMIN_EMAIL:-admin@localhost}'

    restart: unless-stopped
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          cpus: '2'
          memory: 4G
        reservations:
          cpus: '1'
          memory: 2G

    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:3000/"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 10s
      retries: 3
      start_period: 60s

volumes:
  epidbot_data:
    driver: local

docs.title: Environment Variables File (.env)
docs.text:
Create a .env file in the same directory as your docker-compose.yml:

# API Keys
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-openai-key
ZHIPU_API_KEY=your-zhipu-key
DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=your-deepseek-key
GOOGLE_API_KEY=your-google-key

# Session Security (generate with: python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))")
SECRET_KEY=your-secret-key-here

# Default Admin Credentials
EPIDBOT_ADMIN_USER=admin
EPIDBOT_ADMIN_PASSWORD=change_this_immediately
EPIDBOT_ADMIN_EMAIL=admin@yourdomain.com

docs.title: Access Application
docs.text:
Open browser to: http://localhost:3000

Login with your admin credentials.

docs.title: 1. Strong Passwords
docs.text:
Always use strong, unique passwords:

# Generate a secure password
python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(16))"

docs.title: 2. Change Default Password
docs.text:
Immediately after first login, change the admin password:

docker exec -it epidbot uv run python auth_cli.py passwd admin

docs.title: 3. Secure SECRET_KEY
docs.text:
Generate a secure SECRET_KEY:

python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))"

Add to your .env file:

SECRET_KEY=<generated-key>

docs.title: 4. Use Docker Secrets (Swarm)
docs.text:
For Docker Swarm, use secrets instead of environment variables:

secrets:
  epidbot_admin_password:
    external: true

services:
  epidbot:
    secrets:
      - epidbot_admin_password
    environment:
      - EPIDBOT_ADMIN_PASSWORD_FILE=/run/secrets/epidbot_admin_password

docs.title: 5. Restrict Access
docs.text:
Use firewall rules to restrict access to port 3000:

# Only allow from specific IP
ufw allow from 192.168.1.0/24 to any port 3000

docs.title: 6. HTTPS in Production
docs.text: Always use HTTPS in production with a reverse proxy (Nginx, Traefik, Caddy).

docs.title: Cannot Create Default Admin
docs.text:
Problem: Container exits with error about missing password

Solution: Set the EPIDBOT_ADMIN_PASSWORD environment variable

export EPIDBOT_ADMIN_PASSWORD=your-password
docker-compose up -d

docs.title: Cannot Login
docs.text:
Problem: "Authentication failed" when trying to login

Solutions:

  1. Verify user exists: 

    docker exec -it epidbot uv run python auth_cli.py list

  2. Reset password: 

    docker exec -it epidbot uv run python auth_cli.py passwd <username>

  3. Check container logs: 

    docker-compose logs epidbot

docs.title: Database Persistence
docs.text:
Problem: Users disappear after container restart

Solution: Ensure you're using a Docker volume:

volumes:
  - 'epidbot_data:/data'

Check volume exists:

docker volume ls | grep epidbot_data

docs.title: Reset Everything
docs.text:
Warning: This deletes all data!

# Stop container
docker-compose down

# Remove volume
docker volume rm epidbot_epidbot_data

# Start fresh
docker-compose up -d

docs.title: Multiple Admins
docs.text:
Create multiple admins as needed:

# First admin (automatic)
docker-compose up -d

# Additional admins
docker exec -it epidbot uv run python auth_cli.py create-admin

docs.text:
For CI/CD or automated deployments:

#!/bin/bash

docker exec -i epidbot uv run python auth_cli.py create-admin << EOF

password123
password123
researcher1@institute.org
EOF

docker exec -i epidbot uv run python auth_cli.py create-admin << EOF

password456

echo "Users created successfully"

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Clone repository
git clone https://github.com/your-org/epidbot.git
cd epidbot

# Create environment file
cp .env.example .env
# Edit .env with your settings

# Start services
docker compose up -d

# Pull Ollama models
docker exec -it epidbot-ollama ollama pull llama3
docker exec -it epidbot-ollama ollama pull mxbai-embed-large

docs.title: Docker Compose Configuration
docs.text:
version: "3.8"

services:
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    container_name: epidbot-nginx
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./nginx/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
      - ./nginx/ssl:/etc/nginx/ssl:ro
    depends_on:
      - epidbot
      - libby
    networks:
      - epidbot-network

  epidbot:
    build: .
    container_name: epidbot-app
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file:
      - .env
    environment:
      - LIBBY_URL=http://libby:8000
      - OLLAMA_HOST=http://ollama:11434
    volumes:
      - ./data/pysus:/app/data/pysus
      - ./data/plots:/app/plots
    depends_on:
      - libby
      - ollama
    networks:
      - epidbot-network

  libby:
    image: ghcr.io/deeplearn-ped/libby:latest
    container_name: epidbot-libby
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file:
      - .env
    environment:
      - EMBED_DB=duckdb:///data/embeddings.duckdb
      - OLLAMA_HOST=http://ollama:11434
    volumes:
      - ./libby/data:/data
    depends_on:
      - ollama
    networks:
      - epidbot-network

  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama:latest
    container_name: epidbot-ollama
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - ollama-data:/root/.ollama
    networks:
      - epidbot-network
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              count: all
              capabilities: [gpu]

networks:
  epidbot-network:
    driver: bridge

volumes:
  ollama-data:

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text:
FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    curl \
    git \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN pip install uv

COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./
COPY . .

RUN uv sync --frozen

RUN mkdir -p /app/data/pysus /app/plots /app/logs

EXPOSE 3000

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
    CMD curl -f http://localhost:3000/ || exit 1

CMD ["pnpm", "run", "start"]

docs.title: Nginx Configuration
docs.text: Configure Nginx as a reverse proxy for EpidBot.

docs.title: Basic Configuration
docs.text:
Create nginx/nginx.conf:

user nginx;
worker_processes auto;
error_log /var/log/nginx/error.log warn;
pid /var/run/nginx.pid;

events {
    worker_connections 1024;
    use epoll;
    multi_accept on;
}

http {
    include /etc/nginx/mime.types;
    default_type application/octet-stream;

    log_format main '$remote_addr - $remote_user [$time_local] "$request" '
                    '$status $body_bytes_sent "$http_referer" '
                    '"$http_user_agent"';

    access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log main;

    sendfile on;
    tcp_nopush on;
    tcp_nodelay on;
    keepalive_timeout 65;

    # Gzip compression
    gzip on;
    gzip_vary on;
    gzip_proxied any;
    gzip_comp_level 6;
    gzip_types text/plain text/css application/json application/javascript;

    # Rate limiting
    limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=general:10m rate=10r/s;
    limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=api:10m rate=30r/s;

    # Upstreams
    upstream epidbot {
        server epidbot:3000;
        keepalive 32;
    }

    upstream libby {
        server libby:8000;
        keepalive 16;
    }

    # HTTP to HTTPS redirect
    server {
        listen 80;
        server_name _;
        return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
    }

    # HTTPS Server
    server {
        listen 443 ssl http2;
        server_name your-domain.com;

        # SSL
        ssl_certificate /etc/nginx/ssl/fullchain.pem;
        ssl_certificate_key /etc/nginx/ssl/privkey.pem;
        ssl_session_timeout 1d;
        ssl_session_cache shared:SSL:50m;
        ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
        ssl_ciphers ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256;
        ssl_prefer_server_ciphers off;

        # Security headers
        add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000" always;
        add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;
        add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;

        # Max upload size
        client_max_body_size 50M;

        # EpidBot
        location / {
            limit_req zone=general burst=20 nodelay;

            proxy_pass http://epidbot;
            proxy_http_version 1.1;
            proxy_set_header Host $host;
            proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
            proxy_set_header Connection "";

            # WebSocket support
            proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
            proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
            proxy_read_timeout 86400;
        }

        # Libby API
        location /api/kb/ {
            limit_req zone=api burst=50 nodelay;

            rewrite ^/api/kb/search$ /api/retrieve break;
            rewrite ^/api/kb/(.*)$ /api/$1 break;

            proxy_pass http://libby;
            proxy_http_version 1.1;
            proxy_set_header Host $host;
            proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        }

        # Health checks
        location /health/epidbot {
            access_log off;
            proxy_pass http://epidbot/;
        }

        location /health/libby {
            access_log off;
            proxy_pass http://libby/api/health;
        }
    }
}

docs.title: SSL Setup
docs.text: Configure SSL/TLS certificates for secure HTTPS access.

docs.title: Install Certbot
docs.text:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install certbot -y

docs.title: Obtain Certificate
docs.text:
Stop any service on port 80:

# Stop nginx if running
docker compose stop nginx

# Obtain certificate
sudo certbot certonly --standalone -d your-domain.com

# Certificates will be at:
# /etc/letsencrypt/live/your-domain.com/fullchain.pem
# /etc/letsencrypt/live/your-domain.com/privkey.pem

docs.title: Copy to Project
docs.text:
# Create SSL directory
mkdir -p nginx/ssl

# Copy certificates
sudo cp /etc/letsencrypt/live/your-domain.com/fullchain.pem nginx/ssl/
sudo cp /etc/letsencrypt/live/your-domain.com/privkey.pem nginx/ssl/

# Set permissions
sudo chown -R $USER:$USER nginx/ssl/
chmod 600 nginx/ssl/*.pem

docs.title: Auto-Renewal
docs.text:
Create renewal script:

# Create script
cat > renew-ssl.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Renew Let's Encrypt certificate
certbot renew --quiet

# Copy new certificates
cp /etc/letsencrypt/live/your-domain.com/fullchain.pem /opt/epidbot/nginx/ssl/
cp /etc/letsencrypt/live/your-domain.com/privkey.pem /opt/epidbot/nginx/ssl/

# Reload nginx
docker compose -f /opt/epidbot/docker-compose.yml restart nginx
EOF

chmod +x renew-ssl.sh

Add to crontab:

sudo crontab -e

# Add this line (runs monthly at midnight on the 1st)
0 0 1 * * /opt/epidbot/renew-ssl.sh

docs.title: Self-Signed Certificate (Development)
docs.text:
For development/testing only:

# Create SSL directory
mkdir -p nginx/ssl

# Generate self-signed certificate
openssl req -x509 -nodes -days 365 -newkey rsa:2048 \
  -keyout nginx/ssl/privkey.pem \
  -out nginx/ssl/fullchain.pem \
  -subj "/CN=localhost"

Warning

Self-signed certificates will show browser warnings. Only use for development.

docs.title: Certificate expired
docs.text:

openssl x509 -in nginx/ssl/fullchain.pem -noout -dates

sudo cp /etc/letsencrypt/live/your-domain.com/*.pem nginx/ssl/
docker compose restart nginx

docs.title: Security Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use strong ciphers: Only allow TLS 1.2+
  2. Enable HSTS: Force HTTPS connections
  3. Regular renewal: Auto-renew Let's Encrypt
  4. Protect keys: Set restrictive permissions on privkey.pem
  5. Monitor expiration: Set up alerts for certificate expiry

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: EpidBot's architecture uses a microservices approach with NGINX as a reverse proxy, backed by PostgreSQL, DuckDB, and an isolated sandbox container.

docs.title: System Overview
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     NGINX (reverse proxy)                     │
│          SSL termination, static file serving                │
├─────────────────┬───────────────────┤
│  /              │  /api/            │
│  Next.js :3000  │  FastAPI :8123    │
│  (primary UI)   │  (REST + WS API)  │
└─────────────────┴─────────┬─────────┘
                            │
               ┌────────────┼──────────────────┐
               │  PostgreSQL (:5432)            │
               │  users, sessions, messages,    │
               │  api_keys, reports, payments   │
               ├────────────────────────────────┤
               │  DuckDB (in-memory catalog)    │
               │  Parquet metadata indexing      │
               ├────────────────────────────────┤
               │  Sandbox container (:8080)     │
               │  Python/SQL execution, GDAL,   │
               │  rasterio, xarray, rioxarray   │
               └────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Next.js Frontend (frontend/)
docs.text:
Primary user interface built with Next.js 15:

  • React components with Tailwind CSS styling
  • next-intl for internationalization (5 languages)
  • WebSocket client for real-time streaming chat
  • JWT-based authentication with auto-refresh
  • Protected routes via AuthProvider context
  • Session management, admin panel, report downloads

Key pages:

Route Purpose /chat New chat session /chat/[sessionId] Continue existing session /login, /register, /verify-email Authentication & email verification /forgot-password, /reset-password Self-service password reset /auth/callback OAuth social-login callback /admin Users, groups, usage, feature usage, model config, data catalog, skills, pricing, profiles, KB management, Blipper moderation, marketing, newsletter, ads /settings Profile, plan/subscription, Git integrations, Zotero, voice, external agents /reports Report downloads and management (+ /reports/schedules periodic reports, /reports/public/[token] share pages) /sessions Session history /search Dataset/message search /knowledge-base Knowledge base management (documents, wiki, graph) /data My Data — upload and manage user datasets /plots My Plots — browse, edit & run, share, bulk delete, ZIP download /projects Collaborative projects (members, artifacts, tasks, incidents) /blipper Community feed (posts, likes, follows) /favorites Starred reports/plots/datasets /ide In-browser Pyodide code editor

docs.title: FastAPI REST API (epidbot/api/)
docs.text:
Backend API with JWT + API key authentication — ~420 REST endpoints across 35+ routers:

  • REST endpoints: Auth (incl. OAuth, avatars, TOS), chat, sessions, reports (incl. LaTeX/Zenodo/co-authors/reviews), uploads (incl. publish/enrichment), plots (incl. public gallery), admin, search/export, tools, usage, knowledge base (incl. wiki graph), payments, projects, collaboration (presence/activity), comments, reviews, provenance, incidents, tasks, workspace context, favorites, snippets, data files, catalog, share, external agents, jobs, invitations, voice, newsletter, ads, marketing tracking, Blipper feed
  • WebSocket streaming: Real-time chat with tool progress, mid-stream interrupt, heartbeat
  • Background tasks: Job cleanup, sandbox health monitoring
  • Middleware: CORS, quota enforcement, rate limiting, scanner blocking

Key modules:

Module Purpose main.py App factory, CORS, lifespan, routers auth.py JWT creation/verification, password hashing dependencies.py FastAPI auth dependencies (CurrentUser, AdminUser, ApiEnabledUser) websocket.py WebSocket handler for streaming chat gating.py Plan/feature gating for tools and UI routes/auth.py Login, register, token refresh, onboarding, email verification, OAuth, avatars routes/chat.py Chat completion (REST + streaming), message feedback routes/admin.py Admin: users, groups, config, catalog, skills, dream, campaigns, email templates routes/sessions.py Chat session CRUD, sharing, session documents routes/reports.py Report generation, download, sharing, versioning, LaTeX, Zenodo, co-authors routes/uploads.py User dataset upload, preview, publish, enrichment routes/plots.py Plot gallery, upload, sync, public gallery, bulk ops, ZIP download routes/projects.py Projects: items, members, sharing, subscriptions routes/payments.py Payment plans, Asaas integration (PIX + credit card) routes/newsletter*.py Double opt-in newsletter, issues, tips, subscribers, runs routes/periodic_reports.py Scheduled report CRUD and runs routes/search.py Message/code search, session export (PDF, Markdown, etc.) quota.py Token quota enforcement middleware jobs.py Background job manager

docs.title: Agent Core (epidbot/tools/)
docs.text:
Pydantic-AI agent with 310 registered tools that self-register via the @tool decorator into a central registry (epidbot/tool_registry.py). Highlights:

Module Purpose core.py Global state (DATA_PATH), DuckDB connection, onboarding tutorial, tool discovery pysus.py PySUS/DATASUS downloads (atomic + validated), queries, catalog refresh datafiles.py Defective (truncated/corrupt) parquet detection & cleanup analysis.py Statistical analysis tools plotting.py Flexible chart rendering (temporal, spatial, comparison) raster_plotting.py GeoTIFF/raster visualization via rasterio diagrams.py Mermaid diagram generation catalog.py Metadata catalog tools sandbox.py Secure code execution with auto-restart resilience sigtap / tuss_sigtap.py / tuss.py SIGTAP and TUSS nomenclature tools msdados.py Ministry of Health open data (18 ms_get_* tools) malaria_atlas.py 10 tools for Malaria Atlas Project data pathoplexus.py Genomic sequence tools knowledge_base.py KB search and document management mosqlimate.py Infodengue/climate data who.py / worldbank.py / ecdc.py / ecdc_atlas.py / paho.py International surveillance data eurostat.py / undata.py / nz_health.py / ukhsa.py / china_cdc.py More international sources gadm.py / gbif.py Boundaries and biodiversity occurrence data anvisa.py / healthdata_gov.py ANVISA / US HealthData.gov epi.py / advanced_epi.py / causal.py / actuarial.py / surveillance.py / spatial.py Epidemiological methods pubmed.py / crossref.py / openalex.py / semantic_scholar.py / arxiv.py / biorxiv.py / doi.py / zotero.py Literature & references projects.py / git.py / snippets.py / skills.py / external_agents.py Collaboration reports.py / manuscript.py / snippet_builder.py / code_consolidation.py Reporting models.py Structured result models (DownloadResult, ReportResult, …) and tool-name sets progress.py Per-user download serialization and progress events

docs.title: Chat Service (epidbot/services/chat.py)
docs.text:
Core chat orchestration layer:

  • Agent streaming with Pydantic-AI
  • Tool event handling (start, progress, complete, timeout)
  • Image extraction from tool results (PlotResult, DiagramResult)
  • Response splitting for inline image display
  • User-friendly error formatting
  • Sandbox state management

docs.title: Database Layer (epidbot/db/)
docs.text:
PostgreSQL with psycopg connection pool:

Module Purpose connection.py Connection pool management schema.py Table definitions and migrations token_usage.py Token usage tracking

Key tables: users, sessions, messages, message_files, message_feedback, reports, report_files, report_shares, report_versions, api_keys, refresh_tokens, api_jobs, token_usage, payments, outbreak_reports, code_snippets, session_shares, catalog_datasets, plots, groups, user_groups, user_profiles

docs.title: Sandbox Worker (epidbot/sandbox/)
docs.text:
Isolated Docker container for code execution:

  • Python 3.12 with pandas, numpy, duckdb, matplotlib, seaborn, scipy, scikit-learn, lifelines, statsmodels
  • GDAL system libraries for rasterio, xarray, rioxarray
  • HTTP API with /execute/python, /execute/sql, /health
  • Three-layer resilience: retry with backoff, Docker restart, background health monitor

docs.title: Chat Flow (Next.js Frontend)
docs.text:
User types message in Next.js
    │
    ▼
WebSocket send ({type: "start", payload: {message, session_id, locale}})
    │
    ▼
FastAPI WebSocket handler (websocket.py)
    │
    ├──▶ Authenticate user (JWT/API key)
    ├──▶ Validate session ownership
    ├──▶ Create/update session in PostgreSQL
    │
    ▼
Chat Service (services/chat.py)
    │
    ▼
Pydantic-AI Agent (agent.py)
    │
    ├──▶ Tool Selection & Execution
    │       │
    │       ├──▶ PySUS (download)
    │       ├──▶ DuckDB (query)
    │       ├──▶ Sandbox (Python/SQL)
    │       ├──▶ Matplotlib (visualize)
    │       ├──▶ Malaria Atlas (geospatial)
    │       └──▶ Knowledge Base (search)
    │
    ▼ Stream events back via WebSocket
    │
    ├──▶ thinking (agent is reasoning)
    ├──▶ tool_start (tool executing, with progress)
    ├──▶ chunk (streaming response text)
    ├──▶ complete (final response with images)
    ├──▶ error (something went wrong)
    └──▶ turn_interrupted (user sent new message)

docs.title: Mid-stream Interrupt
docs.text:
When a user sends a message during streaming:

  1. WebSocket handler cancels the active streaming task
  2. Partial content is saved as an assistant message
  3. turn_interrupted event is sent to the client
  4. New message starts a fresh turn

docs.title: Sandbox Resilience
docs.text:
Three-layer availability system:

  1. Retry with backoff: On ConnectError, wait 3s and retry once
  2. Docker restart: If retry fails, restart the container via Docker socket
  3. Background health monitor: Every 60s, checks sandbox health and auto-restarts if unhealthy

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
• JWT tokens: 15-minute access token, 7-day refresh token
  • API keys: SHA-256 hashed, prefix-based identification (ek_...)
  • Password hashing: bcrypt via passlib
  • Admin password: Read from ADMIN_PASSWORD env var (default: changeme)

docs.title: Session Validation
docs.text:
• WebSocket connections validate session ownership before streaming
  • Users can only access their own sessions and messages

docs.title: Input Sanitization
docs.text:
• CQL filter parameters in Malaria Atlas tools are sanitized against injection
  • ISO codes validated with regex (^[A-Z]{3}$)
  • SQL queries run in isolated sandbox (no direct DB access)

docs.title: CORS
docs.text:
• Configurable allowed origins (default: localhost:3000, localhost:8123)
  • Credentials allowed for authenticated routes

docs.title: Internationalization
docs.text:
The Next.js frontend uses next-intl with 5 languages:

Locale Language en English pt-BR Portuguese (Brazil) es Spanish zh-CN Chinese ar Arabic

Translation files: frontend/src/messages/{locale}.json

The chat response language is controlled by the locale parameter passed to the WebSocket, which the agent uses for its response language.

docs.title: Documentación de EpidBot
docs.text: EpidBot es un asistente impulsado por IA para analizar datos de salud pública brasileños e internacionales. Proporciona una interfaz de lenguaje natural para descargar, consultar, analizar y visualizar datos de salud de DATASUS, OMS, Banco Mundial, Malaria Atlas Project y muchas otras fuentes.

docs.title: Características
docs.text:
• Interfaz de Lenguaje Natural: Formule preguntas sobre datos de salud en Portugués, Inglés o Español
  • Soporte Multi-idioma: Interfaz completa en Portugués, Inglés, Español, Chino y Árabe
  • Descarga de Datos: Descarga automáticamente datos de PySUS (SINAN, SIM, SIH y más)
  • Consultas SQL: Ejecute consultas DuckDB SQL en archivos parquet
  • Visualizaciones: Genere gráficos, mapas, plots, diagramas y visualizaciones raster
  • Datos Internacionales: OMS, Banco Mundial, ECDC, Mosqlimate, OPS, Malaria Atlas Project, Pathoplexus
  • Base de Conocimiento: Almacene y recupere documentación con embeddings vectoriales
  • Gestión de Sesiones: Mantenga el historial de conversaciones a través de múltiples sesiones
  • Generación de Informes: Cree informes PDF formateados con visualizaciones incrustadas
  • Sandbox Seguro: Ejecute código Python y SQL en un contenedor Docker aislado
  • Tutorial de Onboarding: Los nuevos usuarios reciben un tour guiado automáticamente
  • Mensajes durante Streaming: Envíe mensajes durante el streaming para interrumpir y redirigir
  • Plugin QGIS: Converse con EpidBot dentro de QGIS, con inyección de contexto del mapa y resultados cargados de vuelta como capas
  • API REST: Acceso programático completo vía autenticación JWT/API key
  • WebSocket Streaming: Chat en tiempo real con indicadores de progreso de herramientas

docs.title: Arquitectura
docs.text:
EpidBot está construido con:

  • Next.js — Interfaz web principal (React, Tailwind CSS, next-intl)
  • FastAPI — API REST con soporte WebSocket streaming
  • Pydantic-AI — Framework de agentes para interacciones LLM (50+ herramientas)
  • PostgreSQL — Cuentas de usuario, sesiones, mensajes, claves API
  • PySUS — Descargador de datos de salud brasileños
  • DuckDB — Motor SQL en memoria para consultar archivos parquet
  • Docker — Despliegue en contenedores con aislamiento de sandbox

docs.text:
from epidbot.knowledgebase import LibbyClient

client = LibbyClient()

# Verificar salud
health = client.health_check()
print(health["status"])

# Añadir texto
result = client.add_text(
    text="Información importante de salud...",
    doc_name="health_guide",
    collection_name="epidemiology"
)

# Buscar
results = client.search("síntomas de dengue", num_docs=3)
for doc in results["documents"]:
    print(f"{doc['doc_name']}: {doc['score']}")

docs.title: Despliegue con Docker
docs.text: Despliegue EpidBot usando Docker Compose con Libby y Ollama.

docs.title: Requisitos Previos
docs.text:
• Docker y Docker Compose instalados
  • 8GB+ RAM (16GB recomendado)
  • 50GB+ espacio en disco
  • Nombre de dominio (para producción)

docs.title: Inicio Rápido
docs.text:
# Clonar repositorio
git clone https://github.com/your-org/epidbot.git
cd epidbot

# Crear archivo de entorno
cp .env.example .env
# Editar .env con sus configuraciones

# Iniciar servicios
docker compose up -d

# Descargar modelos Ollama
docker exec -it epidbot-ollama ollama pull llama3
docker exec -it epidbot-ollama ollama pull mxbai-embed-large

docs.title: Configuración de Docker Compose
docs.text:
version: "3.8"

services:
  nginx:
    image: nginx:alpine
    container_name: epidbot-nginx
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"
      - "443:443"
    volumes:
      - ./nginx/nginx.conf:/etc/nginx/nginx.conf:ro
      - ./nginx/ssl:/etc/nginx/ssl:ro
    depends_on:
      - epidbot
      - libby
    networks:
      - epidbot-network

  epidbot:
    build: .
    container_name: epidbot-app
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file:
      - .env
    environment:
      - LIBBY_URL=http://libby:8000
      - OLLAMA_HOST=http://ollama:11434
    volumes:
      - ./data/pysus:/app/data/pysus
      - ./data/plots:/app/plots
    depends_on:
      - libby
      - ollama
    networks:
      - epidbot-network

  libby:
    image: ghcr.io/deeplearn-ped/libby:latest
    container_name: epidbot-libby
    restart: unless-stopped
    env_file:
      - .env
    environment:
      - EMBED_DB=duckdb:///data/embeddings.duckdb
      - OLLAMA_HOST=http://ollama:11434
    volumes:
      - ./libby/data:/data
    depends_on:
      - ollama
    networks:
      - epidbot-network

  ollama:
    image: ollama/ollama:latest
    container_name: epidbot-ollama
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - ollama-data:/root/.ollama
    networks:
      - epidbot-network
    deploy:
      resources:
        reservations:
          devices:
            - driver: nvidia
              count: all
              capabilities: [gpu]

networks:
  epidbot-network:
    driver: bridge

volumes:
  ollama-data:

docs.title: Dockerfile
docs.text:
FROM python:3.12-slim

WORKDIR /app

RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
    build-essential \
    curl \
    git \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN pip install uv

COPY pyproject.toml uv.lock ./
COPY . .

RUN uv sync --frozen

RUN mkdir -p /app/data/pysus /app/plots /app/logs

EXPOSE 3000

HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=5s --retries=3 \
    CMD curl -f http://localhost:3000/ || exit 1

CMD ["pnpm", "run", "start"]

docs.title: Configuración de Nginx
docs.text: Configure Nginx como proxy inverso para EpidBot.

docs.title: Configuración Básica
docs.text:
Cree nginx/nginx.conf:

user nginx;
worker_processes auto;
error_log /var/log/nginx/error.log warn;
pid /var/run/nginx.pid;

events {
    worker_connections 1024;
    use epoll;
    multi_accept on;
}

http {
    include /etc/nginx/mime.types;
    default_type application/octet-stream;

    log_format main '$remote_addr - $remote_user [$time_local] "$request" '
                    '$status $body_bytes_sent "$http_referer" '
                    '"$http_user_agent"';

    access_log /var/log/nginx/access.log main;

    sendfile on;
    tcp_nopush on;
    tcp_nodelay on;
    keepalive_timeout 65;

    # Compresión Gzip
    gzip on;
    gzip_vary on;
    gzip_proxied any;
    gzip_comp_level 6;
    gzip_types text/plain text/css application/json application/javascript;

    # Limitación de tasa
    limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=general:10m rate=10r/s;
    limit_req_zone $binary_remote_addr zone=api:10m rate=30r/s;

    # Upstreams
    upstream epidbot {
        server epidbot:3000;
        keepalive 32;
    }

    upstream libby {
        server libby:8000;
        keepalive 16;
    }

    # Redirección HTTP a HTTPS
    server {
        listen 80;
        server_name _;
        return 301 https://$host$request_uri;
    }

    # Servidor HTTPS
    server {
        listen 443 ssl http2;
        server_name your-domain.com;

        # SSL
        ssl_certificate /etc/nginx/ssl/fullchain.pem;
        ssl_certificate_key /etc/nginx/ssl/privkey.pem;
        ssl_session_timeout 1d;
        ssl_session_cache shared:SSL:50m;
        ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;
        ssl_ciphers ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256;
        ssl_prefer_server_ciphers off;

        # Encabezados de seguridad
        add_header Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=63072000" always;
        add_header X-Frame-Options "SAMEORIGIN" always;
        add_header X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff" always;

        # Tamaño máximo de carga
        client_max_body_size 50M;

        # EpidBot
        location / {
            limit_req zone=general burst=20 nodelay;

            proxy_pass http://epidbot;
            proxy_http_version 1.1;
            proxy_set_header Host $host;
            proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
            proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-Proto $scheme;
            proxy_set_header Connection "";

            # Soporte WebSocket
            proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade;
            proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade";
            proxy_read_timeout 86400;
        }

        # API Libby
        location /api/kb/ {
            limit_req zone=api burst=50 nodelay;

            rewrite ^/api/kb/search$ /api/retrieve break;
            rewrite ^/api/kb/(.*)$ /api/$1 break;

            proxy_pass http://libby;
            proxy_http_version 1.1;
            proxy_set_header Host $host;
            proxy_set_header X-Real-IP $remote_addr;
        }

        # Verificaciones de salud
        location /health/epidbot {
            access_log off;
            proxy_pass http://epidbot/;
        }

        location /health/libby {
            access_log off;
            proxy_pass http://libby/api/health;
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Configuración SSL
docs.text: Configure certificados SSL/TLS para acceso HTTPS seguro.

docs.title: Instalar Certbot
docs.text:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install certbot -y

docs.title: Obtener Certificado
docs.text:
Detenga cualquier servicio en el puerto 80:

# Detener nginx si está ejecutándose
docker compose stop nginx

# Obtener certificado
sudo certbot certonly --standalone -d your-domain.com

# Los certificados estarán en:
# /etc/letsencrypt/live/your-domain.com/fullchain.pem
# /etc/letsencrypt/live/your-domain.com/privkey.pem

docs.title: Copiar al Proyecto
docs.text:
# Crear directorio SSL
mkdir -p nginx/ssl

# Copiar certificados
sudo cp /etc/letsencrypt/live/your-domain.com/fullchain.pem nginx/ssl/
sudo cp /etc/letsencrypt/live/your-domain.com/privkey.pem nginx/ssl/

# Establecer permisos
sudo chown -R $USER:$USER nginx/ssl/
chmod 600 nginx/ssl/*.pem

docs.title: Renovación Automática
docs.text:
Cree script de renovación:

# Crear script
cat > renew-ssl.sh << 'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
# Renovar certificado Let's Encrypt
certbot renew --quiet

# Copiar nuevos certificados
cp /etc/letsencrypt/live/your-domain.com/fullchain.pem /opt/epidbot/nginx/ssl/
cp /etc/letsencrypt/live/your-domain.com/privkey.pem /opt/epidbot/nginx/ssl/

# Recargar nginx
docker compose -f /opt/epidbot/docker-compose.yml restart nginx
EOF

chmod +x renew-ssl.sh

Añada a crontab:

sudo crontab -e

# Añada esta línea (ejecuta mensualmente a medianoche el día 1)
0 0 1 * * /opt/epidbot/renew-ssl.sh

docs.title: Certificado Autofirmado (Desarrollo)
docs.text:
Solo para desarrollo/pruebas:

# Crear directorio SSL
mkdir -p nginx/ssl

# Generar certificado autofirmado
openssl req -x509 -nodes -days 365 -newkey rsa:2048 \
  -keyout nginx/ssl/privkey.pem \
  -out nginx/ssl/fullchain.pem \
  -subj "/CN=localhost"

Warning

Los certificados autofirmados mostrarán advertencias del navegador. Solo use para desarrollo.

# Renovar Let's Encrypt
sudo certbot renew
sudo cp /etc/letsencrypt/live/your-domain.com/*.pem nginx/ssl/
docker compose restart nginx

docs.title: Mejores Prácticas de Seguridad
docs.text:
1. Use cifrados fuertes: Solo permita TLS 1.2+
  2. Habilite HSTS: Fuerce conexiones HTTPS
  3. Renovación regular: Auto-renueve Let's Encrypt
  4. Proteja claves: Establezca permisos restrictivos en privkey.pem
  5. Monitoree expiración: Configure alertas para vencimiento de certificados

docs.title: Autenticación
docs.text: EpidBot utiliza autenticación por usuario/contraseña con gestión segura de sesiones.

docs.title: Descripción General
docs.text: EpidBot requiere autenticación para acceder a la aplicación. Esto garantiza: - Aislamiento de usuarios (cada usuario tiene sus propias sesiones y datos) - Control de acceso seguro - Persistencia de sesiones

docs.title: Características de Seguridad
docs.text:
• Hash de Contraseñas: Todas las contraseñas se hashean usando bcrypt con generación automática de salt
  • Tokens JWT: access tokens de corta duración (HS256, ~30 minutos) renovados automáticamente por refresh tokens de ~7 días, revocables y almacenados en PostgreSQL
  • Claves de API: acceso programático opcional vía X-API-Key
  • OAuth: inicio de sesión social con proveedores configurables

docs.title: Gestión de Usuarios
docs.text: Los usuarios se gestionan a través de la herramienta de línea de comandos auth_cli.py.

docs.title: Configuración Inicial
docs.text:
Antes de iniciar EpidBot por primera vez, cree un usuario administrador:

uv run python auth_cli.py create-admin

Se le solicitará: - Nombre de usuario (obligatorio) - Contraseña (obligatorio, no se mostrará) - Confirmación de contraseña - Email (opcional)

Ejemplo:

$ uv run python auth_cli.py create-admin
=== Create Admin User ===
Username: admin
Password: 
Confirm password: 
Email (optional, press Enter to skip): admin@example.com

✓ Admin user created successfully!
  Username: admin
  User ID: 1
  Email: admin@example.com

docs.title: Creando Usuarios Adicionales
docs.text:
Use el mismo comando create-admin para crear usuarios adicionales:

uv run python auth_cli.py create-admin

docs.title: Listar Todos los Usuarios
docs.text:
uv run python auth_cli.py list

Salida:

=== User List ===

ID    Username             Email                          Created              Last Login          
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1     admin                admin@example.com              2026-03-10           2026-03-10          
2     researcher           researcher@institute.org       2026-03-11           Never               

Total: 2 user(s)

docs.title: Cambiar Contraseña
docs.text:
uv run python auth_cli.py passwd <username>

Ejemplo:

$ uv run python auth_cli.py passwd admin
=== Change Password for 'admin' ===
New password: 
Confirm new password: 

✓ Password changed successfully for user 'admin'

docs.title: Eliminar Usuario
docs.text:
uv run python auth_cli.py delete <username>

Ejemplo:

$ uv run python auth_cli.py delete researcher
=== Delete User 'researcher' ===
⚠️  WARNING: This action cannot be undone!
Type 'yes' to confirm deletion of user 'researcher': yes

⚠️  Note: This will delete the user but preserve their chat history.
    To fully implement user deletion with cascade, database-level constraints need to be updated.

✓ User 'researcher' marked for deletion (manual database cleanup may be required)

docs.title: Via Interfaz Web
docs.text:
1. Inicie EpidBot: cd frontend && pnpm dev
  2. Abra el navegador en http://localhost:3000
  3. Ingrese su nombre de usuario y contraseña
  4. Haga clic en "Login"

docs.title: Gestión de Sesión
docs.text:
• Las sesiones duran 30 días por defecto
  • Permanecerá conectado hasta que la sesión expire o borre las cookies del navegador
  • Cada usuario tiene sesiones aisladas e historial de chat propio

docs.title: SECRET_KEY
docs.text:
La variable de entorno SECRET_KEY se usa para encriptar tokens de sesión:

export SECRET_KEY=su-clave-secreta-aleatoria-aqui

Importante: - Genere una clave aleatoria segura para producción - Mantenga esta clave en secreto - Si la cambia, todas las sesiones existentes serán invalidadas

Para generar una clave segura:

python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))"

Agregue a su archivo .env:

SECRET_KEY=clave-generada-aqui

docs.title: Esquema de Base de Datos
docs.text:
Los usuarios se almacenan en la tabla users en PostgreSQL (epidbot/db/schema.py):

Columna Tipo Descripción id INTEGER ID de usuario (auto-generado) username VARCHAR Nombre de usuario único password_hash VARCHAR Contraseña hasheada con bcrypt email VARCHAR Dirección de email (opcional) avatar_url VARCHAR URL del avatar (opcional) github_id INTEGER ID de GitHub (para OAuth futuro, opcional) created_at TIMESTAMP Fecha de creación de cuenta last_login TIMESTAMP Fecha del último login

docs.title: Para Administradores
docs.text:
1. Use Contraseñas Fuertes: Exija que los usuarios usen contraseñas fuertes y únicas
  2. Limite el Acceso: Cree cuentas solo para usuarios que necesitan acceso
  3. Monitoree el Acceso: Revise regularmente la lista de usuarios con auth_cli.py list
  4. Proteja el SECRET_KEY: Mantenga la clave secreta segura y nunca la confíe al control de versiones
  5. HTTPS en Producción: Siempre use HTTPS en entornos de producción

docs.title: Para Usuarios
docs.text:
1. Contraseñas Fuertes: Use contraseñas fuertes y únicas
  2. Cerrar Sesión: Cierre sesión al usar computadoras compartidas
  3. Proteja sus Credenciales: Nunca comparta su contraseña

docs.title: No Puedo Iniciar Sesión
docs.text:
Problema: Mensaje "Authentication failed"

Soluciones: 1. Verifique la ortografía del nombre de usuario (distingue mayúsculas/minúsculas) 2. Verifique que la contraseña sea correcta 3. Intente restablecer la contraseña: uv run python auth_cli.py passwd <username>

docs.title: Olvidé la Contraseña
docs.text:
Problema: Usuario olvidó la contraseña

Solución: El administrador puede restablecerla:

uv run python auth_cli.py passwd <username>

docs.title: Sesión Expirada
docs.text:
Problema: "Session expired" o desconectado repentinamente

Solución: - Inicie sesión nuevamente - Las sesiones expiran después de 30 días por defecto - Verifique si SECRET_KEY fue cambiado

docs.text: Comando Descripción Ejemplo create-admin Crear un nuevo usuario uv run python auth_cli.py create-admin list Listar todos los usuarios uv run python auth_cli.py list passwd <username> Cambiar contraseña uv run python auth_cli.py passwd admin delete <username> Eliminar usuario uv run python auth_cli.py delete user1

docs.title: Archivo de Configuración
docs.text:
El archivo config.yaml se crea automáticamente en la primera ejecución con valores predeterminados:

# Ruta de almacenamiento de datos PySUS
data_dir: "~/public"

# Idioma de respuesta
language: "Brazilian Portuguese"

# Idioma de la interfaz
ui_language: "pt-BR"

# Proveedor LLM activo
active_provider: "openai"
active_model: "gpt-4o"

# Configuraciones de proveedores
providers:
  openai:
    type: openai
    api_key_env: OPENAI_API_KEY
    default_model: gpt-4o

  ollama:
    type: openai_compatible
    base_url: http://localhost:11434/v1
    default_model: llama3

# Configuración de base de conocimiento
knowledge_base:
  enabled: true
  libby_url: "http://localhost:8000"
  default_collection: "datasus"

# Prompt del sistema (personaliza el comportamiento del agente)
system_prompt: |
  You are an analytical assistant for Brazilian health data (DATASUS/SINAN).
  You can download data using PySUS and query it using DuckDB.
  ...

docs.title: Configuración del Prompt del Sistema
docs.text:
El campo system_prompt define el comportamiento y las instrucciones del agente. Puede personalizarlo para:

  • Cambiar la personalidad o tono del agente
  • Añadir instrucciones específicas del dominio
  • Modificar directrices de uso de herramientas
  • Ajustar preferencias de visualización

docs.title: Variables de Plantilla
docs.text:
El prompt del sistema soporta estas variables de plantilla:

Variable Descripción {data_dir} Ruta al directorio de datos PySUS {language} Configuración de idioma de respuesta {kb_instructions} Instrucciones de base de conocimiento (cuando está habilitado)

Nota: Para incluir llaves literales en su prompt (ej., ejemplos JSON), use llaves dobles: {{ y }}.

docs.title: Ejemplo de Personalización
docs.text:
system_prompt: |
  You are a specialized epidemiologist assistant.

  Focus on:
  - Disease surveillance patterns
  - Outbreak detection
  - Public health recommendations

  Data is stored in: {data_dir}

  Respond in: {language}

  {kb_instructions}

docs.title: Cambiar Proveedores
docs.text:
Via interfaz:

  1. Vaya a la pestaña Configuration
  2. Seleccione el proveedor del menú desplegable
  3. Ingrese el nombre del modelo
  4. Haga clic en Save Configuration

Via archivo de configuración:

active_provider: "ollama"
active_model: "llama3"

docs.title: Rutas de Datos
docs.text:
Estructura predeterminada:

~/pysus/
├── SINAN/
│   ├── DENG/
│   ├── CHIK/
│   └── ZIKA/
├── SIM/
└── SIH/

Ruta personalizada:

data_dir: "/data/health-data"

docs.title: Instalación
docs.text: Esta guía cubre la instalación de EpidBot en su máquina local.

docs.title: Requisitos Previos
docs.text:
• Python 3.12 o superior
  • Gestor de paquetes uv (recomendado) o pip
  • Git
  • (Opcional) Ollama para soporte LLM local

docs.title: Instalar uv
docs.text: curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

docs.title: Clonar el Repositorio
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/your-org/epidbot.git
cd epidbot

docs.title: Instalar Dependencias
docs.text:
Usando uv (recomendado):

uv sync

Usando pip:

pip install -e .

docs.title: Variables de Entorno
docs.text:
Cree un archivo .env en la raíz del proyecto:

# Clave API de OpenAI (requerida para modelos OpenAI)
OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-your-api-key-here

# Opcional: URL de la base de conocimiento Libby
LIBBY_URL=http://localhost:8000

# Opcional: Host de Ollama (para modelos locales)
OLLAMA_HOST=http://localhost:11434

docs.title: Ejecutar la Aplicación
docs.text:
cd frontend && pnpm dev

La aplicación estará disponible en http://localhost:3000.

docs.title: Configuración de Ollama (Opcional)
docs.text:
Para soporte LLM local:

# Instalar Ollama
curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh

# Descargar un modelo
ollama pull llama3
ollama pull mxbai-embed-large  # Para embeddings de la base de conocimiento

docs.title: Base de Conocimiento Libby (Opcional)
docs.text:
Para la funcionalidad de base de conocimiento, ejecute el servidor Libby:

# Instalar libby
pip install libby

# Ejecutar el servidor
libby-server
