docs.text: Recurso Limite Tempo de execução 300 segundos máximo Memória Configurável CPU Configurável

docs.title: Estrutura do Código
docs.text:
# Importar bibliotecas primeiro
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

# Carregar dados
df = pd.read_parquet('/data/pysus/arquivo.parquet')

# Processar
result = df.groupby('coluna').agg({'valor': 'sum'})

# Saída
print(result.to_markdown())

docs.title: Tratamento de Erros
docs.text:
try:
    df = pd.read_parquet('/data/pysus/arquivo.parquet')
    if df.empty:
        print("Nenhum dado encontrado")
    else:
        print(f"Carregadas {len(df)} linhas")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Erro: {e}")

docs.title: Ferramentas SIGTAP & TUSS
docs.text: Ferramentas para as nomenclaturas de procedimentos brasileiras: SIGTAP (Sistema de Gerenciamento da Tabela de Procedimentos, Medicamentos, Órteses, Próteses e Complementos da Saúde) e TUSS (Terminologia Unificada da Saúde Suplementar, da ANS).

docs.title: Ferramentas SIGTAP
docs.text:
O SIGTAP é publicado pelo DATASUS em competições mensais, com arquivos de texto de largura fixa divididos em ~41 tabelas (procedimentos, ocupação, financiamento, complexidade, etc.).

Ferramenta Descrição list_sigtap_competencies Lista as competições mensais disponíveis para download download_sigtap_data Baixa e converte uma competência da SIGTAP list_sigtap_tables Lista as tabelas disponíveis com contagem de linhas describe_sigtap_table Mostra o layout de colunas de uma tabela search_sigtap_procedures Busca procedimentos por nome get_sigtap_procedure Detalhes completos de um procedimento query_sigtap SQL somente-leitura sobre as tabelas da SIGTAP 
Quais competências da SIGTAP estão disponíveis?
Procure procedimentos de hemodiálise na SIGTAP

docs.title: Ferramentas TUSS
docs.text:
A TUSS é mantida pela ANS e organizada em tabelas (terminologias) expostas pela API OCL da ANS. Os downloads são cacheados localmente; exportações pré-carregadas acompanham a implantação, garantindo consultas mesmo quando a API da ANS está lenta.

Ferramenta Descrição list_tuss_tables Lista as terminologias TUSS search_tuss_codes Busca códigos dentro de uma tabela get_tuss_code Consulta um código TUSS específico list_tuss_concepts Navega pelos conceitos de uma tabela import_tuss_export Importa/atualiza uma exportação TUSS pré-carregada

docs.title: Tabelas Relacionadas da ANS (TUSS × SIGTAP)
docs.text: Ferramenta Descrição download_ans_related_table Baixa uma tabela relacionada da ANS (cruzamento TUSS × SIGTAP ou erros TISS) query_ans_related_table SQL somente-leitura sobre a tabela relacionada find_tuss_sigtap_mapping Vincula códigos TUSS e SIGTAP pelo cruzamento oficial

docs.title: Exemplo
docs.text: Qual o código TUSS equivalente ao procedimento SIGTAP 0301010014?

docs.title: Notas
docs.text:
• Todas as ferramentas de consulta (query_sigtap, query_ans_related_table) são somente-leitura.
  • As ferramentas SIGTAP têm timeout de 300s, pois o download de uma competência nova converte 41 tabelas.

docs.title: Consultas SQL
docs.text:
Para usuários avançados, consultas SQL diretas via DuckDB:

SELECT 
    ID_MUNICIP,
    COUNT(*) as cases
FROM read_parquet('~/pysus/SINAN/DENG.parquet')
WHERE year = 2023
GROUP BY ID_MUNICIP
ORDER BY cases DESC
LIMIT 10

docs.title: Sintaxe de Filtros
docs.text:
Filtros usam formato JSON:

[
  {"column": "year", "operator": "gte", "value": 2020},
  {"column": "UF", "operator": "eq", "value": "SP"}
]

Operadores:

Operador Descrição eq Igual a ne Diferente de gt Maior que gte Maior ou igual a lt Menor que lte Menor ou igual a in Em lista between Intervalo like Correspondência de padrão is_null É nulo is_not_null Não é nulo

docs.title: Base de Conhecimento

docs.text:
A base de conhecimento usa Libby para:

docs.title: Detecção de Duplicatas
docs.text:
O sistema verifica automaticamente duplicatas:

  • URLs são verificadas por domínio + caminho
  • Documentos de texto são verificados por nome
  • Documentos divididos em chunks (ex: doc_part1) são reconhecidos

docs.title: Divisão em Chunks
docs.text:
Documentos grandes são divididos automaticamente:

  • Tamanho máximo de chunk: 1024 caracteres
  • Sobreposição: 100 caracteres
  • Limites de parágrafos são preservados

docs.title: LibbyClient
docs.text:
from epidbot.knowledgebase import LibbyClient

client = LibbyClient()

# Adicionar texto
client.add_text(
    text="Content to embed",
    doc_name="my_document",
    collection_name="datasus"
)

# Adicionar página web
client.add_webpage(
    url="https://example.com",
    collection_name="datasus"
)

# Buscar
results = client.search(
    query="SINAN notification fields",
    collection_name="datasus",
    num_docs=5
)

# Listar documentos
docs = client.list_documents(collection_name="datasus")

# Verificar existência
exists = client.document_exists("my_document", "datasus")

docs.title: Melhores Práticas
docs.text:
1. Use coleções apropriadas: Organize documentos por tópico
  2. Adicione fontes ricas em metadados: Documentação oficial funciona melhor
  3. Verifique antes de adicionar: Evite conteúdo duplicado
  4. Verifique embeddings: Use busca para confirmar que o conteúdo está acessível
  5. Manutenção regular: Periodicamente revise e limpe as fontes

docs.title: Plugin QGIS
docs.text:
O plugin QGIS do EpidBot traz o assistente para dentro do QGIS, permitindo fazer perguntas epidemiológicas, gerar gráficos e carregar resultados geoespaciais no seu mapa sem sair do fluxo de trabalho em SIG.

O plugin conversa com a sua conta EpidBot pela mesma API REST da interface web, então sessões, gráficos, cotas e base de conhecimento permanecem sincronizados. É open source em github.com/Deeplearn-PeD/epidbot-qgis-plugin sob licença GPL-2.0-or-later.

docs.title: Requisitos
docs.text:
• QGIS 3.28 ou mais recente (Windows, macOS ou Linux)
  • Uma conta EpidBot em plano pago (Pro, Max ou Equipe) — as chaves de API estão incluídas em todos
  • Uma chave de API pessoal do EpidBot — crie em Configurações > Chaves de API na interface web (veja REST API)
  • Acesso de rede ao servidor do EpidBot (https://api.epidbot.kwar-ai.com.br por padrão)

docs.title: Pelo repositório oficial de plugins do QGIS (recomendado)
docs.text:
1. No QGIS, abra Complementos > Gerenciar e Instalar Complementos
  2. Busque por EpidBot (ID 6764) ou abra a página do plugin
  3. Clique em Instalar complemento
  4. Ative o painel EpiDBot Chat em Ver > Painéis ou clique no botão da barra de ferramentas

Instalado assim, o plugin se atualiza pelo próprio gerenciador de complementos do QGIS.

docs.title: A partir de um arquivo ZIP
docs.text:
Use apenas quando precisar de uma versão mais nova que a publicada no repositório:

  1. Baixe o epidbot.zip mais recente
  2. No QGIS, abra Complementos > Gerenciar e Instalar Complementos > Instalar a partir de ZIP
  3. Selecione o arquivo e clique em Instalar complemento

docs.title: Configuração
docs.text:
Clique no botão ⚙ (engrenagem) do painel de chat:

Configuração Significado URL do servidor URL base da API do EpidBot — preenchida com https://api.epidbot.kwar-ai.com.br Chave de API Sua chave pessoal, enviada no cabeçalho X-API-Key em cada requisição. Guardada no keyring do sistema quando o pacote opcional keyring está disponível Idioma das respostas Idioma das respostas do assistente: en ou pt-BR Intervalo de consulta Segundos entre consultas de status do job (padrão 1,5 s)

docs.title: Conversando pelo QGIS
docs.text:
O painel EpiDBot Chat, ancorável, funciona como o chat web:

  • As respostas trazem Markdown, tabelas e miniaturas de gráficos
  • Escolha uma sessão existente, inicie outra ou deixe o servidor criar uma; ao trocar de sessão o histórico é recarregado, incluindo gráficos
  • Exporte a conversa para um arquivo Markdown
  • A interface do painel existe em inglês e português do Brasil, e as requisições rodam em thread de segundo plano para o QGIS continuar responsivo

docs.title: Integração com o mapa
docs.text:
• Injeção de contexto do mapa — cada prompt carrega automaticamente as camadas ativas (com nomes de campos, valores de amostra e seleções), a extensão do canvas em EPSG:4326 e o CRS do projeto, para o assistente saber o que está na sua tela
  • Prompts espaciais — ações de um clique perguntam sobre a extensão atual ou as feições selecionadas
  • Adicionar ao mapa — blocos GeoJSON e URLs de conjuntos de dados nas respostas viram camadas estilizadas no canvas com um clique

Exemplos de prompts:

Mapeie a incidência de dengue dos municípios carregados no meu projeto

Qual é a população total dos municípios selecionados?

docs.title: Trabalhando com gráficos
docs.text:

docs.title: Actuarial Modeling Tools
docs.text:
Actuarial analysis using chainladder, GEMAct and lifelines — loss reserving from run-off triangles, collective-risk claim costing, portfolio loss aggregation with reinsurance, and parametric lifetime/mortality models.

These tools are gated behind the advanced_analysis feature (Pro plan and above).

docs.title: estimate_loss_reserves
docs.text:
Project a run-off triangle to ultimate and estimate outstanding claim reserves (IBNR). Reports age-to-age LDFs and CDFs, per-origin latest/ultimate/reserve, totals, and Mack standard errors, with an actual-vs-projected development plot.

estimate_loss_reserves(
    ctx: RunContext[None],
    dataset_path: str,              # one row per triangle cell
    origin_column: str,             # accident period (year or date)
    development_column: str,        # lag (age mode) or calendar period
    value_column: str,              # paid or incurred losses
    cumulative: bool = True,        # False for incremental triangles
    method: str = "chainladder",    # "chainladder" | "bornhuetter_ferguson" | "cape_cod"
    development_mode: str = "age",  # "age" | "calendar"
    lag_unit: str = "periods",      # "periods" | "months" | "years"
    ldf_average: str = "volume",    # "volume" | "simple" | "regression" | "geometric"
    tail: str = "none",             # "none" | "curve" | "bondy" | "clark" | "constant"
    apriori: Optional[float] = None,      # expected loss ratio (BF only)
    premium_column: Optional[str] = None, # exposure (BF / Cape Cod)
    group_column: Optional[str] = None,   # separate triangle per group
) -> str

Notes:

  • chainladder works with premiums alone; bornhuetter_ferguson needs apriori (expected loss ratio) and premium_column; cape_cod needs premium_column and estimates the a priori loss ratio from the data.
  • development_column is usually an integer lag (lag 1 = first period). Ages given in months (12, 24, …) need lag_unit="months". Calendar-period columns need development_mode="calendar".
  • Tail factors extrapolate development beyond the last observed age — only meaningful for triangles that are not fully developed.

docs.title: fit_claim_loss_model
docs.text:
Fit claim severity and frequency distributions by maximum likelihood and price the aggregate claim cost with GEMAct's collective risk model (FFT): expected loss, VaR/TVaR, and the pure premium of a deductible/limit (XL) layer.

fit_claim_loss_model(
    ctx: RunContext[None],
    dataset_path: str,                # one row per claim (or per period with count_column)
    amount_column: str,               # individual claim amount (> 0)
    count_column: Optional[str] = None,   # claims per period → Poisson vs NegBinom
    severity_dist: str = "auto",      # "auto" | "lognormal" | "gamma" | "weibull" | "genpareto" | "exponential"
    frequency_dist: str = "auto",     # "auto" | "poisson" | "nbinom"
    deductible: float = 0.0,          # per-claim deductible
    cover: Optional[float] = None,    # per-claim limit
    var_level: float = 0.995,         # VaR/TVaR level
) -> str

Severity candidates are fitted with the location fixed at 0 and compared by AIC (KS p-value reported). Frequency is Poisson unless counts are overdispersed (variance > 1.5 × mean), which selects the negative binomial.

docs.title: aggregate_portfolio_loss
docs.text:
Aggregate loss distribution from parametric components — no dataset needed. Collective risk model $X = Z_1 + \dots + Z_N$ approximated by FFT, Panjer recursion or (quasi-)Monte Carlo, with exact reinsurance pricing.

aggregate_portfolio_loss(
    ctx: RunContext[None],
    frequency_dist: str = "poisson",      # "poisson" | "nbinom" | "geom" | "binom"
    frequency_params_json: str = '{"mu": 10}',
    severity_dist: str = "lognormal",     # gemact severity name
    severity_params_json: str = '{"scale": 5000, "shape": 1.2}',
    method: str = "fft",                  # "fft" | "recursion" | "mc" | "qmc"
    deductible: float = 0.0,              # XL priority
    cover: Optional[float] = None,        # XL limit
    share: float = 1.0,                   # quota-share proportion ceded
    aggr_deductible: float = 0.0,         # stop-loss aggregate deductible
    aggr_cover: Optional[float] = None,   # stop-loss aggregate cover
    var_level: float = 0.995,
) -> str

Parameters use GEMAct's parameterisation (lognormal: scale = exp(μ), shape = σ of the underlying normal). Typical use: pass the distributions fitted by fit_claim_loss_model and price an XL layer on top.

docs.title: fit_lifetime_model
docs.text:
Parametric lifetime/mortality model with AIC selection, median lifetime and life expectancy (restricted mean survival time to a horizon), plus survival and hazard plots.

fit_lifetime_model(
    ctx: RunContext[None],
    dataset_path: str,              # one row per subject
    duration_column: str,           # time-to-event (or censoring)
    event_column: str,              # 1 = event, 0 = censored
    model: str = "auto",            # "auto" or a specific model (see below)
    covariates_json: Optional[str] = None,  # JSON array of numeric columns → AFT
    horizon: Optional[float] = None,        # RMST horizon (default: max observed)
) -> str

Without covariates the candidates are exponential, Weibull, log-normal, log-logistic and generalised gamma; with covariates the AFT variants (Weibull/LogNormal/LogLogistic) are compared. Interpret exp(coef) as time acceleration factors.

docs.title: Demonstration prompt
docs.text:
Paste the following into a new chat to generate a report that exercises all four tools. The data-generation script is seeded and reproducible; it was validated against the tool implementations.

Produce an end-to-end demonstration of your actuarial modeling tools on
synthetic data and finish with a shareable report. Follow every step in
order and do not skip any.

## Step 1 — Generate the synthetic datasets

Run this code in the Python sandbox (execute_python_code), exactly as
written:

```python
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

rng = np.random.default_rng(42)

# 1. Run-off triangle: cumulative paid claims, 12 accident years x 12 lags.
ages = np.arange(1, 13)
dev_prop = 1 - np.exp(-((ages / 4.2) ** 1.35))
volume = 5_000_000 * 1.05 ** np.arange(12)
rows = []
for i in range(12):
    for j in range(12):
        if i + j + 1 > 12:
            continue
        expected = volume[i] * 0.78 * dev_prop[j]
        paid = rng.lognormal(np.log(expected) - 0.5 * 0.04**2, 0.04)
        rows.append({
            "accident_year": 2013 + i,
            "dev_lag": j + 1,
            "cumulative_paid": round(float(paid), 2),
            "earned_premium": round(float(volume[i] * 1.25), 2),
        })
tri = pd.DataFrame(rows)
tri.to_parquet("/workspace/claims_triangle.parquet", index=False)

# 2. Claims 2023-2024: overdispersed monthly counts, lognormal severity.
lam = rng.gamma(2.0, 9.0, 24)
claims = []
for p, k in enumerate(lam):
    for amount in rng.lognormal(9.0, 1.1, int(k)):
        claims.append({"month": p + 1, "amount": round(float(amount), 2)})
cl = pd.DataFrame(claims)
cl = cl.merge(cl.groupby("month").size().rename("n_claims").reset_index(), on="month")
cl.to_parquet("/workspace/claims_2024.parquet", index=False)

# 3. Annuitant lives: lognormal log-time survival with right-censoring.
n = 800
age0 = rng.normal(72, 6, n).clip(55, 95)
sex = rng.integers(0, 2, n)
log_t = 2.48 - 0.03 * (age0 - 72) + 0.25 * sex + 0.5 * rng.normal(0, 1, n)
t_death = np.exp(log_t)
t_cens = rng.uniform(2, 35, n)
lives = pd.DataFrame({
    "time_observed": np.minimum(t_death, t_cens).round(2),
    "died": (t_death <= t_cens).astype(int),
    "age": age0.round(1),
    "sex": sex,
})
lives.to_parquet("/workspace/annuitant_lives.parquet", index=False)

print(f"triangle: {len(tri)} cells, {tri.accident_year.nunique()} accident years")
print(f"claims:   {len(cl)} claims over {cl.month.nunique()} months")
print(f"lives:    {len(lives)} subjects, {int(lives.died.sum())} deaths")
```

Expected output: a 78-cell 12x12 run-off triangle, ~360 claims over 24
months, and 800 annuitant lives with ~40% censoring.

## Step 2 — Persist the datasets

Save each file with `save_to_user_data` (dataset names: `claims_triangle`,
`claims_2024`, `annuitant_lives`) and use the dataset paths returned by
each call in the steps below.

## Step 3 — Loss reserving (chainladder)

Run `estimate_loss_reserves` twice on the triangle dataset:

a) Chain-ladder: `origin_column="accident_year"`,
   `development_column="dev_lag"`, `value_column="cumulative_paid"`,
   `method="chainladder"`.
b) Cape Cod: same columns, `method="cape_cod"`,
   `premium_column="earned_premium"`.

Report the LDFs, the per-origin reserve table (with Mack standard errors
from run a) and compare the two total reserves.

## Step 4 — Claim costing (collective risk model)

Run `fit_claim_loss_model` on `claims_2024` with
`amount_column="amount"`, `count_column="n_claims"`, `deductible=5000`,
`cover=50000`, `var_level=0.995`. Report the fitted severity (AIC/KS)
and frequency distributions, the expected aggregate loss, VaR/TVaR, and
the pure premium of the XL 50k xs 5k layer.

## Step 5 — Portfolio aggregation & reinsurance

Run `aggregate_portfolio_loss` using the parameters fitted in step 4:
`frequency_dist="nbinom"` with its fitted `n`/`p` JSON, and
`severity_dist="lognormal"` with its fitted `scale`/`shape` JSON;
`method="fft"`, `deductible=5000`, `cover=50000`. Confirm that the
ceded pure premium matches step 4's layer premium (it should, to
rounding).

## Step 6 — Lifetime modeling

Run `fit_lifetime_model` on `annuitant_lives` with
`duration_column="time_observed"`, `event_column="died"`,
`covariates_json='["age", "sex"]'`. Report the AIC comparison, the
selected parameters, and interpret exp(coef) as time acceleration
factors (e.g. what exp(mu_ sex) means for female vs male annuitants),
plus median lifetime and life expectancy.

## Step 7 — The report

Use `generate_structured_report` with:

- title: "Actuarial Modeling Demonstration with EpidBot"
- language: "en", report_type: "analysis"
- abstract: 2-3 paragraphs covering the objective (demonstrate loss
  reserving, claim costing, portfolio aggregation and lifetime
  modeling), the methods, the headline findings (both reserve estimates,
  the fitted severity distribution, VaR 99.5%, the ceded premium, and
  the sex acceleration factor), and an explicit statement that all data
  are synthetic.
- Sections — embed each tool's figure via its markdown image syntax and
  include the key result tables:
  1. "Introduction" — purpose and scope of the demonstration
  2. "Synthetic Data" — the three datasets and how they were generated
  3. "Loss Reserving" — LDF table, per-origin reserve table, the
     chain-ladder development figure, and the chain-ladder vs Cape Cod
     comparison
  4. "Claim Severity and Frequency" — the severity fit figure, fit
     diagnostics table, aggregate loss metrics
  5. "Portfolio Aggregation and Reinsurance" — the aggregate loss
     distribution figure, VaR table, ceded vs retained premium
  6. "Lifetime and Mortality Modeling" — the survival/hazard figure,
     AFT parameter table, median lifetime and life expectancy
  7. "Conclusions" — what the exercise demonstrates
  8. "Limitations" — synthetic data with simplified data-generating
     processes; results illustrate tool usage and are NOT suitable for
     real-world pricing or reserving decisions.
- Use LaTeX for ALL math ($...$ inline, $$...$$ display). Never use raw
  Unicode math symbols.
- Do NOT add a References section: the report makes no external
  scientific claims (all data are synthetic).

docs.title: Expected results (seed 42)
docs.text:
For verification, the validated run of this prompt produces approximately:

  • Chain-ladder total reserve ≈ 21.0M vs Cape Cod ≈ 21.1M (ELR estimated at ≈ 0.64)
  • Severity: lognormal, scale ≈ 8151, shape ≈ 1.11 (true $e^9 \approx 8103$, $\sigma = 1.1$)
  • Frequency: negative binomial (mean ≈ 18 claims/month, variance ≈ 51)
  • XL 50k xs 5k ceded premium ≈ 171k, identical in steps 4 and 5
  • Lifetime: lognormal AFT selected; $\exp(\mu_{\text{age}}) \approx 0.970$ per year of entry age; $\exp(\mu_{\text{sex}}) \approx 1.26$ (females longer-lived), both $p < 0.001$; life expectancy ≈ 15 years to horizon

docs.title: Advanced Epidemiological Methods Tools
docs.text:
Methodological tools beyond basic queries: association measures, transmission modelling, causal inference, decision modelling, outbreak detection, spatial statistics, disease burden and meta-analysis.

Many of these are gated to the Pro plan (advanced_analysis); the rest are open. All tools return tables and, where applicable, charts saved to My Plots.

docs.title: Epidemiological Measures (open)
docs.text: Tool Description estimate_association_measures OR / RR / IRR with confidence intervals standardize_population_rates Age-standardized rates and SMR evaluate_screening_test Sensitivity, specificity, PPV/NPV, kappa estimate_seroprevalence_tool Seroprevalence with test-performance correction analyze_vaccination_coverage_tool Vaccination coverage and dropout

docs.title: Transmission Modelling (open)
docs.text: Tool Description run_epidemic_model Simulate compartmental models (SIR/SEIR and variants) calibrate_epidemic_model Calibrate a model to observed incidence estimate_effective_reproduction_number Estimate Rt from incidence data

docs.text: Tool Description construct_causal_dag Draw a causal DAG diagram estimate_difference_in_differences Causal effect via DiD estimate_interrupted_time_series Intervention effects via ITS estimate_propensity_score Propensity score matching or weighting estimate_panel_regression Fixed-effects panel regression

docs.text: Tool Description build_decision_tree Build and evaluate a decision tree run_markov_model Markov state-transition model evaluate_cost_effectiveness Compare strategies on the cost-effectiveness plane run_sensitivity_analysis Sensitivity analysis (tornado diagram or PSA)

docs.title: Anomaly Detection Tools
docs.text:
Unsupervised anomaly (outlier) detection using PyOD — the most comprehensive Python library for outlier detection.

While EARS/CUSUM surveillance detects temporal aberrations on case series and spatial tools find geographic clusters, these tools flag unusual individual records across many numeric variables at once: municipalities with impossible case counts, reporting glitches, or emerging signals that deviate from the historical regime.

docs.title: detect_anomalies
docs.text:
Scores every row of a dataset for "how unusual" it is and highlights the most anomalous records. Returns the anomaly summary, a score distribution histogram, a scatter plot (PCA projection) with anomalies highlighted, an optional score-over-time plot (when a date column is given), the top-N most anomalous rows as a table, and the full per-row scores saved to the My Data page.

detect_anomalies(
    ctx: RunContext[None],
    dataset_path: str,
    method: str = "auto",            # see table below
    columns_json: str = None,        # numeric columns, e.g. '["cases","incidence"]'
    filters_json: str = None,        # SQL WHERE fragments, e.g. '["year >= 2020"]'
    contamination: float = 0.05,     # expected fraction of anomalies (0 < c < 0.5)
    n_neighbors: int = None,         # lof/knn neighbour count (default 20)
    date_column: str = None,         # enables the score-over-time plot
    top_n: int = 20,                 # rows listed in the table
) -> str

docs.title: Choosing a method
docs.text:
method="auto" (recommended) fits a four-detector ensemble — ECOD + COPOD + HBOS + Isolation Forest — and combines their scores by standardized average, which is robust across most data shapes. Individual methods:

Method When to use Notes iforest Strong general-purpose default Handles large tables ecod / copod Skewed count data (epidemiological totals) Very fast, no tuning hbos Wide tables (many columns) Histogram-based, fastest lof / knn Anomalies are locally rare Distance-based; ≤100k rows cblof Small detached clusters Clustering-based ocsvm Tight "normal" regime One-class SVM pca / mcd Correlated features Linear models mad Univariate check on one column z-score threshold, contamination ignored

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Automatic scan of a weekly case series: 

Run anomaly detection on the weekly dengue dataset using case count and incidence;
plot the scores over the epi-week column and list the 20 most unusual weeks.

Targeted univariate check: 

Use MAD to check the "deaths" column of the SINAN 2024 dataset for outliers.

docs.title: Reading the output
docs.text:
• Score distribution — how well separated the flagged anomalies are; a long right tail is normal, a flat blob suggests the data has no strong outliers.
  • Score over time — anomalies clustered together in time often indicate a real signal (outbreak start, reporting change) rather than isolated glitches.
  • Anomaly rate far from contamination — with method="auto" the rate tracks the contamination parameter; individual detectors may disagree, which is itself informative.
  • The saved CSV (anomaly_score, is_anomaly, plus the original numeric columns) can be joined back to the source dataset via row order for deeper inspection.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Non-numeric and all-NA columns are skipped automatically; remaining NAs are median-imputed before scoring.
  • Numeric coercion is attempted on selected columns (e.g. numeric strings are converted).
  • The tool is gated to the Pro plan (advanced_analysis), like the other advanced analysis tools.
  • In scheduled reports, tick "Include anomaly detection" — each run then executes detect_anomalies on the schedule's datasets and adds an Anomalies section to the generated report.

docs.title: Collaboration & Workspace Tools
docs.text: Tools for organizing work into projects, working with Git repositories, reusing code snippets and skills, and delegating to external agents.

docs.title: Projects
docs.text:
Projects group related artifacts — sessions, reports, figures and datasets — under one roof with per-member access. Managed in the UI under Projects; these tools let the agent organize artifacts for you.

Tool Description list_projects List the user's projects create_project Create a new project add_to_project Link a session, report, figure or dataset to a project remove_from_project Unlink an artifact from a project get_project_details Show a project and its linked artifacts

Projects support roles (project_roles is a Pro feature), sharing and subscriptions — see the Projects section of the manual.

docs.title: Git Integrations
docs.text:
Read and write access to the user's GitHub/GitLab repositories from the chat. Read tools are gated to Pro (git_tools); write tools additionally require git_write.

Read (Pro):

Tool Description git_list_repositories List the user's GitHub/GitLab repositories git_get_repository Get metadata for one repository git_list_repository_files List files in a repository git_get_file_content Read a file's content git_list_branches List branches git_list_commits List recent commits git_list_issues List issues git_get_issue Get one issue git_list_pull_requests List PRs (GitHub) / merge requests (GitLab) git_clone_repository Clone a repository into the session workspace

Write (Pro + git_write):

Tool Description git_create_issue Create an issue git_comment_on_issue Comment on an issue git_create_pull_request Open a PR (GitHub) / merge request (GitLab)

Repositories are connected per-user in Settings → Git Integrations.

docs.title: Code Snippets
docs.text:
Tool Description save_code_snippet Save a reusable code snippet search_code_snippets Search saved snippets list_code_snippets List all snippets

Snippets are also produced automatically by plotting/analysis tools so results can be re-run in the in-browser IDE.

docs.title: Skills
docs.text:
Tool Description list_skills List all skills search_skills Search skills by keyword get_skill_content Get the full content of a skill

Skills are curated prompt playbooks (methodology guides) the agent can consult; admins manage them in Admin → Skills.

docs.title: External Agents
docs.text:
Tool Description query_external_agent Send a message to a user-registered external agent and return its reply

External agents (e.g. a local nanobot or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) are registered per-user in Settings → External Agents with a base URL and Bearer token (encrypted at rest). Messages are sent via /v1/chat/completions. Gated to the external_agents feature (Pro).

docs.text: Tools for downloading and querying Brazilian health data, as well as user-uploaded datasets.

docs.title: DATASUS Download Tools (PySUS)
docs.text:
All DATASUS downloads go through PySUS and are saved as parquet under {data_dir}/<SYSTEM>/, in the RO-Crate layout <NAME>/data.parquet, and registered in the catalog automatically.

Downloads are atomic and validated: data is written to a temporary file, the parquet footer/row-count is verified, and only then is the file moved into place. A cached file that fails validation (e.g. left truncated by an interrupted download) is deleted and re-downloaded on the next request.

docs.title: download_health_data
docs.text:
Download SINAN notifiable-disease data.

download_health_data(
    ctx: RunContext[None],
    disease_code: str,  # e.g., "DENG", "CHIK", "ZIKA"
    year: int,          # e.g., 2023
) -> DownloadResult

Example usage: 

Baixe os dados de Dengue para 2023

Supported disease codes (subset):

Code Disease DENG Dengue CHIK Chikungunya ZIKA Zika FEBAM Yellow Fever MALA Malaria TUBE Tuberculosis HANS Hanseníase

Nationwide datasets (e.g. dengue) are downloaded in chunks and merged via DuckDB to keep memory bounded.

docs.title: Other DATASUS systems
docs.text:
Tool System Args download_sim_data SIM — mortality state, year download_sinasc_data SINASC — live births state, year download_sih_data SIH — hospital admissions state, year, month, group download_sia_data SIA — outpatient procedures state, year, month, group download_cnes_data CNES — health establishments state, year, month download_pni_data PNI — immunization state, year download_ciha_data CIHA — hospitalization records state, year, month 
Baixe as internações hospitalares (SIH) de SP em janeiro de 2023

A SIH month ships four file families with different schemas. download_sih_data downloads one family at a time via the group parameter:

Group Family RD (default) AIH Reduzida — the actual hospital admissions table RJ AIH Rejeitada — rejected admissions SP Serviços Profissionais — professional services payments ER AIH Rejeitada com Erro — rejected with errors ALL Merge all families into one wide table (legacy layout)

Files are named SIH{group}{UF}{YY}{MM}.parquet (e.g. SIHRDRJ2501.parquet); ALL keeps the legacy SIH{UF}{YY}{MM} name. The merge uses union_by_name, so newer columns (e.g. FONTE_ORC) are absorbed automatically.

SIA works the same way: a month ships twelve families with different schemas, downloaded one at a time via group — PA (Produção Ambulatorial, the main outpatient-procedures table, default), BI, AD, AM, AN, AQ, AR, AB, AC, AT, PS, SA, or ALL (legacy combined layout). Files: SIA{group}{UF}{YY}{MM}.parquet (e.g. SIAPARJ2501.parquet).

Other tools' files are named <SYSTEM><UF><YY>[(MM)].parquet (e.g. SIMSP23.parquet). Repeat requests detect existing downloads and skip re-downloading.

docs.title: Filter Syntax
docs.text:
Filters are JSON arrays:

[
  {"column": "year", "operator": "gte", "value": 2020},
  {"column": "UF", "operator": "eq", "value": "SP"}
]

Operators:

Operator Description Example eq Equals {"column": "UF", "operator": "eq", "value": "SP"} ne Not equals {"column": "UF", "operator": "ne", "value": "RJ"} gt Greater than {"column": "age", "operator": "gt", "value": 18} gte Greater or equal {"column": "year", "operator": "gte", "value": 2020} lt Less than {"column": "age", "operator": "lt", "value": 65} lte Less or equal {"column": "year", "operator": "lte", "value": 2023} in In list {"column": "UF", "operator": "in", "value": ["SP", "RJ"]} between Range {"column": "age", "operator": "between", "value": [18, 65]} like Pattern match {"column": "name", "operator": "like", "value": "%Silva%"} is_null Is null {"column": "date", "operator": "is_null", "value": true}

docs.title: Duplicate Detection
docs.text:
The system automatically checks for duplicates before adding:

  • Text documents by name

Example response: 

Source already exists in knowledge base: 'portalsinan.saude.gov.br_o-sinan'

docs.title: Chunking
docs.text:
Large documents are automatically split:

  • Maximum chunk size: 1024 characters
  • Overlap: 100 characters
  • Paragraph boundaries preserved

Successfully embedded 'portalsinan.saude.gov.br_o-sinan' (7 chunks) into 
collection 'datasus'.

docs.title: Literature & Reference Tools
docs.text: Tools for searching scholarly literature and building verified bibliographies. Every search tool returns abstract snippets so the agent can verify claims before citing; references are saved to a report's bibliography and can be exported to BibTeX or Zotero.

docs.title: Search Tools
docs.text: Tool Source Description search_pubmed PubMed/NCBI Biomedical literature with abstract snippets search_crossref CrossRef 150M+ scholarly works by keyword search_semantic_scholar Semantic Scholar ~200M papers, any discipline search_arxiv arXiv Open-access preprints (modelling, statistics, CS) search_preprints bioRxiv / medRxiv Epidemiology & public-health preprints filter_openalex OpenAlex Structured metadata filtering with abstract snippets list_zotero_collections Zotero List collections across the user's configured libraries

docs.title: Metadata & Verification Tools
docs.text:
Use these to fetch the full record for one known work — citation plus abstract — before saving it to a report.

Tool Description get_pubmed_citation / get_pubmed_citations One or many PubMed IDs, citations with abstracts get_pubmed_abstract Full abstract of a PubMed article get_crossref_metadata Full citation metadata for a DOI (CrossRef registrant) resolve_doi Resolve ANY DOI to full citation metadata (any registrant) get_openalex_work Formatted OpenAlex citation with full abstract get_semantic_scholar_paper Full paper metadata by any identifier get_arxiv_paper Full metadata for one arXiv ID get_preprint_details Full metadata for a bioRxiv/medRxiv DOI

docs.title: Professional Profile
docs.text: build_professional_profile assembles a researcher profile from ORCID and Google Scholar — publications, metrics and affiliations — useful for report author blocks and collaboration scoping.

docs.title: Typical Workflow
docs.text:
Encontre referências sobre transmissão de dengue por Aedes albopictus,
verifique-as e adicione à bibliografia do meu relatório.
  1. search_pubmed — find candidates with abstract snippets
  2. get_pubmed_citations — fetch full records for the shortlist
  3. save_report_references — save verified references to the report
  4. format_pubmed_bibliography — render the numbered bibliography

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Search/metadata tools have a 300s timeout; NCBI rate limits are respected automatically.
  • Literature search results are truncated to the global max_tool_output_chars cap — ask for narrower queries rather than full listings.

docs.title: Multivariate Analysis Tools
docs.text:
Exploratory multivariate data analysis using prince — dimensionality-reduction methods that summarise many correlated variables into a few components.

These tools complement the analysis tools (which answer targeted questions about specific columns) by revealing the overall structure of a dataset: clusters of similar rows, groups of correlated variables, and which variables drive the most variation.

docs.title: run_multivariate_analysis
docs.text:
Explore multivariate structure via dimensionality reduction. Returns a scree plot (variance explained), a factor map (row + column positions on the first two axes), and a written summary of eigenvalues and the variables that define each component.

run_multivariate_analysis(
    ctx: RunContext[None],
    dataset_path: str,
    method: str,                       # "auto" | "pca" | "ca" | "mca" | "famd" | "mfa"
    columns_json: str,                 # JSON array of columns, e.g. '["age","income","cases"]'
    n_components: int = 2,
    filters_json: Optional[str] = None,  # JSON array of SQL WHERE fragments
    color_by: Optional[str] = None,      # column whose values colour the row points
    groups_json: Optional[str] = None,   # MFA only: {"group": [cols], ...}
) -> str

docs.title: Choosing a method
docs.text:
method="auto" inspects the column types and picks the right method for you (recommended). You can also set it explicitly:

Method When to use Data type PCA Numerical columns only (case counts, rates, demographics) All numeric MCA Categorical columns only (sex, race, diagnosis from SINAN) All categorical, >2 cols CA A two-way contingency table Exactly 2 categorical cols FAMD Mix of numerical and categorical (most real DATASUS tables) Mixed MFA Columns organised into blocks (e.g. demographic block + clinical block) Grouped

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Automatic method on mixed data: 

Find the main axes of variation in the dengue 2023 dataset using age, sex, region and case count.

Explicit PCA on numeric variables: 

Run a PCA on the numerical columns: population, cases, deaths, incidence_rate

MCA on SINAN categorical fields: 

Do an MCA on sex, race, schooling and diagnosis of the tuberculosis data.

MFA with grouped columns: 

Run an MFA grouping the columns into "demographics" (age, sex) and "clinical" (diagnosis, severity).
With groups_json = '{"demographics": ["age","sex"], "clinical": ["diagnosis","severity"]}'.

docs.title: Reading the output
docs.text:
• Scree plot: the bar heights show how much variance each component captures; the red line is the cumulative total. The first 2–3 components should explain a meaningful share (e.g. >60%).
  • Factor map (PCA/FAMD): a correlation circle — arrows point in the direction each variable loads on the two components. Long arrows = strong contribution; arrows pointing the same way = positively correlated variables; opposite = negatively correlated.
  • Symmetric map (MCA/CA/MFA): red X markers are the column categories; grey dots are the rows. Categories plotted close together co-occur.
  • Summary: lists % variance explained per component and the top contributing variables for each, so the LLM (and you) can interpret what the axes represent.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Rows with missing values in the selected columns are dropped before fitting (prince has no NA handling).
  • Integer columns are coerced to float automatically (prince's FAMD treats only float-dtype columns as quantitative).
  • For large datasets (>100k rows), consider aggregating to a coarser level first for better performance.

docs.title: Sandbox Execution Tools
docs.text: Tools for executing Python code and SQL queries in a secure sandbox environment.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
EpidBot provides a secure sandbox for executing arbitrary Python code and SQL queries. The sandbox:

  • Runs in an isolated Docker container
  • Provides access to common data science and geospatial libraries
  • Supports timeouts to prevent runaway code (max 300 seconds)
  • Returns figures as base64-encoded images or saved files
  • Auto-restarts on failure with three-layer resilience

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
The sandbox runs as a separate Docker container. Ensure it's running:

# Check sandbox health
docker ps | grep sandbox

# Or ask EpidBot: "Check sandbox health"

Environment Variable: 

SANDBOX_URL=http://localhost:8080

In Docker Compose, set to the container name: 

SANDBOX_URL=http://epidbot-sandbox:8080

docs.title: execute_python_code
docs.text:
Execute Python code in the secure sandbox.

execute_python_code(
    ctx: RunContext[None],
    code: str,          # Python code to execute
    timeout: int = 240  # Max execution time (1-300 seconds)
) -> str

Parameters:

Name Type Default Description code str required Python code to execute timeout int 240 Max execution time (max 300s)

Available Libraries:

Library Purpose pandas Data manipulation numpy Numerical computing duckdb SQL queries matplotlib Plotting seaborn Statistical visualization scipy Scientific computing scikit-learn Machine learning statsmodels Statistical modeling lifelines Survival analysis mosqlient Mosqlimate data access & forecasting geopandas Geospatial data operations mapclassify Classification schemes (NaturalBreaks, HeadTailBreaks) libpysal Spatial weights & graphs esda Exploratory spatial data analysis rasterio GeoTIFF/raster I/O xarray Multi-dimensional arrays rioxarray Raster data with xarray PIL Image processing

The variable DATA_PATH is available in the sandbox pointing to the data directory.

The variable epidbot_api is available as a restricted HTTP client to call the EpidBot API from sandbox code. It is pre-configured with the internal API secret and supports:

Method Description epidbot_api.get(path, params=, json=, headers=) HTTP GET epidbot_api.post(path, json=, headers=) HTTP POST epidbot_api.put(path, json=, headers=) HTTP PUT epidbot_api.delete(path, headers=) HTTP DELETE

Responses have .status_code, .json(), and .text.

resp = epidbot_api.get('/api/v1/catalog/search', params={'q': 'dengue'})
print(resp.status_code, resp.json())

Available Environment Variables:

When the agent generates code that uses mosqlient to download data, the following API key is already configured in the sandbox environment:

Variable Purpose MOSQLIMATE_API_KEY Mosqlimate platform API key

These can be accessed via os.environ: 

import os
key = os.environ.get("MOSQLIMATE_API_KEY", "")

Example - Data Analysis: 

import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_parquet(f'{DATA_PATH}/dengue_2023.parquet')
print(f"Total rows: {len(df)}")
print(df.describe())

Example - Visualization: 

import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

df = pd.read_parquet(f'{DATA_PATH}/dengue_2023.parquet')
df['month'] = pd.to_datetime(df['DT_NOTIFIC']).dt.month

monthly = df.groupby('month').size()
monthly.plot(kind='bar')
plt.title('Monthly Cases')
plt.savefig('/output/plot.png')

docs.title: execute_sql_query
docs.text:
Execute SQL queries in the sandbox environment.

execute_sql_query(
    ctx: RunContext[None],
    query: str,                    # SQL query (DuckDB syntax)
    database_path: Optional[str],  # Path to DuckDB database
    timeout: int = 240
) -> str

Parameters:

Name Type Default Description query str required SQL query (DuckDB SQL syntax) database_path str None Optional DuckDB file path timeout int 240 Max execution time

Querying Parquet Files:

SELECT
    UF,
    COUNT(*) as total_cases
FROM read_parquet('/data/pysus/dengue_2023.parquet')
GROUP BY UF
ORDER BY total_cases DESC
LIMIT 10

Querying Multiple Files:

SELECT
    year,
    COUNT(*) as cases
FROM read_parquet('/data/pysus/dengue_*.parquet')
GROUP BY year
ORDER BY year

docs.title: Isolation
docs.text:
• Code runs in a separate Docker container
  • No access to host filesystem (except mounted data volumes)
  • Network access can be restricted

docs.title: Resource Limits
docs.text: Resource Limit Execution time 300 seconds max Memory Configurable via Docker CPU Configurable via Docker

docs.title: Data Access
docs.text: Data files are mounted in the sandbox: - /data/pysus/ - PySUS data directory (read-write) - /data/output/ - Output directory for saved figures (per-session workspace)

docs.title: Resilience
docs.text:
The sandbox has a three-layer availability system:

  1. Retry with backoff: On connection failure, waits 3 seconds and retries once
  2. Docker restart: If retry fails, automatically restarts the container via Docker socket
  3. Background health monitor: Every 60 seconds, checks sandbox health and auto-restarts if unhealthy

This ensures the sandbox recovers from crashes, OOM kills, and network issues without manual intervention.

docs.title: SIGTAP & TUSS Tools

Together they let the agent answer questions like "what is procedure 0301010014?", "which TUSS codes map to this SIGTAP procedure?" and "run SQL over this month's SIGTAP release".

docs.text: TUSS is maintained by ANS and organized as a set of tables (terminologies) exposed through the ANS OCL API. Downloads are cached locally; pre-seeded exports are deployed with the app so queries work even when the ANS API is slow.

docs.title: import_tuss_export
docs.text: Import or refresh a pre-seeded TUSS export for offline/local queries.

docs.title: ANS Related Tables (TUSS × SIGTAP)
docs.text:
Three tools expose the official ANS related tables — most importantly the TUSS × SIGTAP crosswalk and the TISS error-code table.

Tool Description download_ans_related_table Download an ANS related table (crosswalk or TISS errors) to a local parquet query_ans_related_table Run read-only SQL over a downloaded related table find_tuss_sigtap_mapping Link TUSS and SIGTAP procedure codes via the official crosswalk

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
Qual o código TUSS equivalente ao procedimento SIGTAP 0301010014?

The agent calls find_tuss_sigtap_mapping and returns the official TUSS counterpart(s), noting the competency the mapping is valid for.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• SIGTAP tools are gated by the category default timeout (300s) because a fresh release download parses 41 archives.
  • All query tools (query_sigtap, query_ans_related_table) are read-only; write statements are rejected.
  • TUSS data is refreshed with import_tuss_export; the deployment playbook auto-downloads fresh exports (see deploy.md).

docs.title: Chat Interface
docs.text: The chat interface is the primary way to interact with EpidBot.

docs.title: Accessing the Chat
docs.text:
Navigate to /chat in your browser. If you're not logged in, you'll be redirected to the login page.

  • New chat: Go to /chat or click "New Chat" in the sidebar
  • Continue session: Click on a previous session in the sidebar, or navigate to /chat/{sessionId}

docs.title: Chat Window
docs.text:
Displays the conversation history with:

  • User messages (right-aligned)
  • Assistant responses (left-aligned, with markdown rendering)
  • Images (plots, maps, and visualizations displayed inline)
  • Tool progress (real-time indicators when tools are running)

docs.title: Tool Progress Indicators
docs.text:
When the agent executes tools, you'll see:

  • Tool name and elapsed time
  • Code preview for sandbox/SQL executions
  • Completion status (success, error, or timeout)

docs.title: Input Box
docs.text:
Type your question and press Enter or click Send.

Mid-stream Messaging

You can send a new message while the assistant is still streaming. The current response will be interrupted and saved, and a new turn will begin with your new message.

docs.title: Voice Input
docs.text:
Click the microphone button inside the input field to use voice input. Speak naturally and your words will be transcribed in real time. Click the microphone again to stop recording. The recognized language follows your interface locale (configurable under Settings → Voice).

On browsers without built-in speech recognition (e.g., Firefox), the microphone automatically falls back to server-side transcription: your audio is sent to the EpidBot server, transcribed, and inserted into the input box. This requires the server's voice feature to be enabled; on a spinning state, the transcription is in flight.

docs.title: Read Aloud & Auto-read
docs.text: Each assistant message has a read aloud button in its action bar. Enable Auto-read in the chat toolbar (or Settings → Voice) to have responses spoken as they stream in, sentence by sentence. Code blocks, tables, and formulas are skipped — only the prose is read. Reading speed and voice can be configured under Settings → Voice; when the server offers natural (synthesized) voices, you can choose them there too.

docs.title: Voice Mode
docs.text: Open hands-free Voice mode from the chat toolbar or with Ctrl+Shift+V (Esc closes it). Voice mode loops continuously: it listens while you speak, a natural pause sends your message, spoken status updates play while the assistant works ("Let me check the data."), and the response is read aloud as it streams. While the assistant speaks, tap anywhere to interrupt and speak again — the assistant handles mid-stream interruptions natively. If the assistant asks a clarifying question, it is read aloud and your spoken answer is sent as the reply.

docs.title: Session Sidebar
docs.text: The session sidebar on the left side of the chat can be collapsed by clicking the collapse button in its header, giving you more space for the conversation. Click the expand button to bring it back.

docs.title: Suggestion Cards
docs.text: When you start a new chat, the welcome screen displays analysis starter templates — clickable suggestion cards with common analysis prompts such as "Analyze dengue trends" or "Compare health indicators." Click any card to immediately start an analysis.

docs.title: Onboarding Tutorial
docs.text:
New users automatically receive a guided tutorial on their first visit. The tutorial introduces:

  1. Available datasets and data sources
  2. How to download and query data
  3. International health data analysis
  4. Visualization capabilities
  5. Tips for complex analyses

The tutorial triggers automatically when a new user with no previous sessions opens the chat.

docs.title: Editing Messages
docs.text: You can edit your last sent message by hovering over it and clicking the pencil icon. Edit the text in the inline editor and press Enter to resubmit. EpidBot will discard the previous response and generate a new one based on your edited message. Press Escape to cancel.

docs.title: Message Feedback
docs.text: After EpidBot responds, hover over an assistant message to reveal thumbs up and thumbs down buttons. Click to rate the quality of the response. Click the same rating again to remove it. This feedback helps improve the system over time.

docs.title: Exporting Chat
docs.text:
Click the Export PDF button at the top of the chat to download the entire conversation as a formatted PDF document, including all messages, embedded images, and formatting.

You can also export sessions from the Sessions page in multiple formats: Markdown, JSON, HTML, plain text, and PDF.

docs.title: Code Blocks
docs.text: Code blocks are syntax-highlighted with a dark theme. Hover over a code block to reveal a copy button that copies the code to your clipboard.

docs.title: Data Tables
docs.text:
Tables rendered in responses include hover actions:

  • Copy as TSV — copies table data to clipboard in tab-separated format
  • Download CSV — downloads table data as a CSV file

docs.title: Markdown Rendering
docs.text:
Responses support:

  • Bold and italic text
  • Lists (numbered and bulleted)
  • Code blocks with syntax highlighting
  • Tables with copy and download actions
  • Mathematical notation (KaTeX)
  • Inline images (plots, maps, diagrams)

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text: Shortcut Action Enter Send message Shift+Enter New line Ctrl+K Open search Ctrl+N Start new session Ctrl+Shift+E Export chat as PDF Ctrl+Shift+V Toggle voice mode Escape Close lightbox / cancel edit / exit voice mode

docs.title: Interactive Cards
docs.text:
Besides plots and tables, the chat can render interactive cards:

  • Clarifying questions — when the agent needs a decision from you, it shows clickable option cards (also spoken in voice mode)
  • Continue analysis — suggested next steps you can trigger with one click
  • Task progress — a live checklist for long, multi-step turns
  • Suggestion cards — starter prompts on the empty chat page

docs.title: Connection Status
docs.text:
A status indicator appears below the input when the WebSocket connection is not active:

  • Reconnecting...: Connection lost, automatically retrying with exponential backoff
  • The send button is always available — messages are queued when offline and sent on reconnection

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Start with data discovery: Check what's available before complex queries
  2. Be specific about years: Always specify the year(s) of interest
  3. Request visualizations: The agent works best when asked to create charts
  4. Use sessions: Create separate sessions for different analyses
  5. Ask in any language: English, Portuguese, and Spanish are well-supported
  6. Edit to refine: Edit your last message to adjust parameters without retyping
  7. Consult external agents: If you have registered an external agent (e.g. a nanobot instance) in Settings > External Agents, you can ask EpiDBot to contact it — e.g. "Consult my agent named my-nanobot and ask: what models are available for dengue forecasting?" EpiDBot sends the message to the agent's OpenAI-compatible API and relays the response back into the conversation.

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text:
If an error occurs:

  • A user-friendly message is displayed in the chat
  • Common issues include quota limits, sandbox timeouts, or data not found
  • You can retry by sending the message again
  • Unanswered messages show an amber banner with a Retry button

Example error: 

The AI model's API quota has been exceeded.
Please try again later or contact the administrator.

docs.title: Knowledge Base
docs.text: The Knowledge Base allows you to store and retrieve documentation about DataSUS, epidemiology, and related topics.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The knowledge base uses Libby for:

  • Document embedding (vector storage)
  • Semantic search
  • Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)

docs.title: Status Check
docs.text: Click Check Status to verify the Libby server is running.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
1. Enter a search query
  2. Select a collection (or "All Collections")
  3. Click Search

Results show relevant document excerpts with relevance scores.

docs.title: Add Sources (Administrator Only)
docs.text:
Adding content to the knowledge base is restricted to administrators. Regular users have read-only access: searching the knowledge base and browsing collections and sources is available to everyone.

Administrators can add content in three ways:

docs.title: Web Pages
docs.text:
1. Enter the URL
  2. Select a collection
  3. Click Add Web Page

The system will:

  1. Fetch the webpage
  2. Extract text content
  3. Split into chunks if needed
  4. Embed and store

docs.title: Text Content
docs.text:
1. Paste text content
  2. Provide a document name
  3. Select a collection
  4. Click Add Text

docs.title: Upload Documents
docs.text:
1. Select a document file (PDF, TXT, Markdown, DOC or DOCX)
  2. Choose a collection
  3. Click Upload & Embed

docs.title: Manage Sources
docs.text:
• List Sources: View all embedded documents
  • List Collections: View collections with document counts

docs.title: Wiki & Knowledge Graph
docs.text:
The Knowledge Base page also hosts the Wiki tab: an agent-maintained knowledge wiki per collection, with an interactive knowledge graph.

  • Graph view — explore nodes (concepts, datasets, documents) and their relationships; free on all plans
  • Ask the graph — explain, path and neighbors queries over the graph
  • Consolidation — the agent periodically distills chat-derived knowledge into wiki pages (admin-managed: rebuild, lint, ingest)

Admins manage wiki consolidation and graph rebuilds under Admin → Wiki Management.

docs.title: Collections
docs.text: Collection Purpose datasus Official DATASUS documentation epidemiology Epidemiological methods and concepts methodology Research methodology

docs.title: Agent Integration
docs.text:
The agent can:

  • Search: Query the knowledge base for relevant information
  • Add sources: Automatically add valuable web resources
  • List sources: See what documentation is available

docs.title: Example Queries
docs.text:
Search the knowledge base for SINAN field definitions

Add this page to the knowledge base: https://portalsinan.saude.gov.br/

What sources are available in the knowledge base?

docs.title: Duplicate Detection
docs.text:
The system automatically checks for duplicates:

  • URLs are checked by domain + path
  • Text documents are checked by name
  • Chunked documents (e.g., doc_part1) are recognized

docs.title: Chunking
docs.text:
Large documents are automatically split:

  • Maximum chunk size: 1024 characters
  • Overlap: 100 characters
  • Paragraph boundaries are preserved

docs.title: LibbyClient
docs.text:
from epidbot.knowledgebase import LibbyClient

client = LibbyClient()

# Add text
client.add_text(
    text="Content to embed",
    doc_name="my_document",
    collection_name="datasus"
)

# Add webpage
client.add_webpage(
    url="https://example.com",
    collection_name="datasus"
)

# Search
results = client.search(
    query="SINAN notification fields",
    collection_name="datasus",
    num_docs=5
)

# List documents
docs = client.list_documents(collection_name="datasus")

# Check existence
exists = client.document_exists("my_document", "datasus")

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Use appropriate collections: Organize documents by topic
  2. Add metadata-rich sources: Official documentation works best
  3. Check before adding: Avoid duplicate content
  4. Verify embeddings: Use search to confirm content is accessible
  5. Regular maintenance: Periodically review and clean up sources

docs.title: My Data
docs.text: The My Data page lets you upload, manage, and preview your own datasets for private analysis alongside public data sources like DATASUS and WHO.

docs.title: Accessing My Data
docs.text: Click My Data in the sidebar navigation.

docs.title: Supported Formats

Format Extension Notes CSV .csv Comma-separated values OpenDocument Spreadsheet .ods LibreOffice/OpenOffice Excel .xlsx, .xls Microsoft Excel GeoJSON .geojson, .json Geographic JSON Shapefile .zip Zipped Shapefile bundle (.shp, .dbf, .shx, .prj) GeoPackage .gpkg OGC GeoPackage

Maximum file size: 50 MB

docs.title: Upload Steps
docs.text:
1. Click the upload area or drag and drop a file
  2. Optionally add a description for your dataset
  3. The file is automatically converted to Parquet format and registered in the catalog
  4. The dataset appears in your list with row count, file size, and column info

docs.title: Browsing Datasets
docs.text:
The dataset list shows each file with:

  • Filename (original upload name)
  • Row count and file size
  • Upload date
  • Description (if provided)

docs.title: Search and Sort

  • Sort controls: Sort by Name, Rows, Size, or Date in ascending or descending order
  • The list shows a count: "N datasets found"

docs.title: Previewing Data
docs.text: Click a dataset to expand it. Two tabs are available:

docs.title: Schema Tab
docs.text:
Shows column-level metadata:

Field Description Column Name Name of the column Data Type DuckDB data type (VARCHAR, INTEGER, DOUBLE, etc.) Nullable Whether the column allows NULL values

docs.title: Preview Tab
docs.text:
Displays the first 10 rows of data in a scrollable table:

  • Maximum 15 columns shown initially (with horizontal scroll for wider datasets)
  • Cell values truncated to 200 characters
  • Shows total row/column counts and number of truncated columns

docs.title: Managing Datasets
docs.text: Action How Edit description Click the description text to add or modify Download Click Download to export the dataset as a CSV (regenerated from the stored Parquet) Refresh metadata Click Refresh to re-register with the catalog Delete Click Delete (confirms before deleting)

docs.title: Analysis Results
docs.text:
When you ask EpidBot to export the results of an analysis (for example, "export the top 100 records to CSV"), the file is automatically saved to your My Data page. It appears in the list alongside your uploads, and you can download it as CSV using the Download button or query it directly in the chat.

SELECT * FROM read_parquet('/data/private/<your_id>/<dataset_name>/data.parquet')

docs.title: Using Uploaded Data in Chat
docs.text:
Once uploaded, your datasets are available for analysis in the chat:

What datasets have I uploaded?

Query my uploaded CSV for the top 10 records by case count

Analyze the regional distribution in my uploaded data

EpidBot can query your uploaded data using DuckDB SQL, just like public datasets.

docs.title: My Plots
docs.text: The My Plots page provides a gallery of all your generated and uploaded visualizations in one place.

docs.title: Accessing My Plots
docs.text: Click My Plots in the sidebar navigation.

docs.title: Browsing Plots
docs.text:
Plots are displayed as a card grid. Each card shows:

  • Thumbnail image preview
  • Filename (e.g., dengue_trend.png)
  • Description (if provided)
  • Source — chat (generated during analysis) or upload (manually uploaded)
  • File size and dimensions (width × height)

docs.title: Search
docs.text: Use the search bar to filter plots by filename or description.

docs.title: Lightbox Preview
docs.text:
Click any plot image to open a full-size lightbox preview that:

  • Scales to 90% of the viewport or the image's natural size (whichever is smaller)
  • Centers the image with a dark semi-transparent overlay
  • Press Escape or click outside the image to close
  • Body scroll is locked while the lightbox is open

docs.title: Uploading Images
docs.text:
Upload your own images to the plot gallery:

  1. Click the Upload button
  2. Select an image file
  3. Allowed types: PNG, JPG, WebP, GIF, SVG (max 20 MB)
  4. Optionally add a description

Uploaded images are stored in your private plot directory.

docs.title: Syncing from Chat History
docs.text:
Click the Sync button to scan all your chat sessions for image references. Any plots found in messages that are not yet in your gallery will be registered automatically. This is useful if:

  • You generated plots in older sessions
  • Plots were created before the My Plots feature was added
  • Plot files were accidentally removed from the gallery

The sync operation reports the number of newly registered and restored plots.

docs.title: Managing Plots
docs.text:
Action How Copy reference Click Copy to copy the markdown image reference (e.g., ![plot](plots/dengue_trend.png)) Edit & run Open the plot's code in the in-browser IDE, tweak and re-run it Add to project Attach the plot to a project Favorite Star a plot — favorites are collected on the Favorites page Share Send the plot to Blipper or copy a share link Edit description Click the description text to add or modify Delete Click Delete (removes from gallery and deletes file from disk)

Bulk actions (multi-select delete) and a download-as-ZIP option are available from the toolbar.

docs.title: Public gallery
docs.text: A curated gallery of plots published by other users is available (GET /plots/public). You can import a public plot into your own gallery with one click (POST /plots/add-from-public).

docs.title: Using Plots in Reports
docs.text:
Plots from the gallery can be referenced in chat and embedded in PDF reports:

Include the dengue trend plot in my report

List available plots

docs.title: API Access
docs.text:
All plot operations are available via the REST API:

  • GET /plots/ — List plots
  • POST /plots/upload — Upload an image
  • POST /plots/sync — Sync from chat history
  • GET /plots/{id}/file — Serve image file
  • GET /plots/{id}/snippet — Snippet that generated the plot
  • PATCH /plots/{id} — Update description
  • DELETE /plots/{id} — Delete plot
  • POST /plots/bulk-delete — Delete multiple plots
  • POST /plots/download-zip — Download plots as a ZIP
  • GET /plots/public / GET /plots/public/file — Public gallery
  • POST /plots/add-from-public — Import a public plot

See REST API Reference for full endpoint details.

docs.title: QGIS Plugin
docs.text:
The EpidBot QGIS plugin brings the assistant inside QGIS, so you can ask epidemiological questions, generate charts and load geospatial results onto your map without leaving your GIS workflow.

The plugin talks to your EpidBot account over the same REST API as the web interface, so sessions, plots, quotas and knowledge base stay in sync. It is open source at github.com/Deeplearn-PeD/epidbot-qgis-plugin under GPL-2.0-or-later.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• QGIS 3.28 or newer (Windows, macOS or Linux)
  • An EpidBot account on a paid plan (Pro, Max or Team) — API keys are included in all of them
  • A personal EpidBot API key — create one in the web interface under Settings > API Keys (see REST API)
  • Network access to the EpidBot server (https://api.epidbot.kwar-ai.com.br by default)

docs.title: From the official QGIS plugin repository (recommended)
docs.text:
1. In QGIS, open Plugins > Manage and Install Plugins
  2. Search for EpidBot (plugin ID 6764) or open the plugin page
  3. Click Install Plugin
  4. Enable the EpiDBot Chat panel from View > Panels, or click its toolbar button

Installed this way, the plugin updates itself through the QGIS plugin manager.

docs.title: From a ZIP package
docs.text:
Use this only for a version newer than the one already published in the repository:

  1. Download the latest epidbot.zip
  2. In QGIS, open Plugins > Manage and Install Plugins > Install from ZIP
  3. Select the file and click Install Plugin

docs.title: Configuring
docs.text:
Click the ⚙ (gear) button in the chat panel:

Setting Meaning Server URL EpidBot API base URL — pre-filled with https://api.epidbot.kwar-ai.com.br API key Your personal key, sent as an X-API-Key header on every request. Stored in the system keyring when the optional keyring package is available Answer language Language of the assistant's answers: en or pt-BR Status poll interval Seconds between job-status polls (default 1.5 s)

docs.title: Chatting from QGIS
docs.text:
The dockable EpiDBot Chat panel works like the web chat:

  • Answers render with Markdown, tables and inline chart thumbnails
  • Pick an existing session, start a new one, or let the server create one; switching sessions reloads the history, including plots
  • Export a conversation to a Markdown file
  • The panel UI is available in English and Brazilian Portuguese, and requests run on a background thread so QGIS stays responsive

docs.title: Map integration
docs.text:
• Map context injection — every prompt automatically carries your active layers (with field names, sample values and current selections), the canvas extent in EPSG:4326 and the project CRS, so the assistant knows what you are looking at
  • Spatial prompts — one-click actions ask about the current extent or the selected features
  • Add to map — GeoJSON blocks and dataset URLs in answers become styled layers on the canvas with a single click

Example prompts:

Map the dengue incidence of the municipalities currently loaded in my project

What is the total population of the selected municipalities?

docs.title: Working with plots
docs.text:
Every chart generated in the plugin can be:

  • Saved to disk as an image file
  • Opened in the system image viewer
  • Embedded in a print layout — added to an "EpidBot Plots" layout for map compositions

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Fix Unauthorized in the panel The API key is missing or invalid. Click ⚙, paste a key created in Settings > API Keys Cannot reach the server Check the Server URL in the plugin settings and your proxy configuration. Transient network failures are retried automatically Panel does not appear Enable it in View > Panels > EpiDBot Chat, or check Plugins > Manage and Install Plugins that the plugin is enabled

docs.title: Sessions
docs.text: EpidBot supports multiple chat sessions with persistent history, sharing, and export.

docs.title: Sessions Page
docs.text:
Click Sessions in the sidebar to see all your conversations. Each session card displays:

  • Session name
  • Message count
  • Last activity time (e.g., "2 hours ago")
  • Shared badge if the session has been shared with or by others

docs.title: Session Actions
docs.text: Button Action New Session Create a new conversation Rename Rename the current session (pencil icon) Delete Delete the current session (trash icon, with confirmation) Resume Click the session card to open the conversation

docs.title: Collapsible Sidebar
docs.text: In the chat view, the session sidebar can be collapsed by clicking the collapse button in its header. This gives you more space for the chat. Click the expand button to bring it back.

docs.title: Sharing Sessions
docs.text:
You can share sessions with other EpidBot users:

  1. Click the share icon on a session card
  2. Type a username in the dialog (autocomplete will suggest matches)
  3. Choose a permission level:
  4. Can view — read-only access to the conversation
  5. Can edit — full access to continue the conversation
  6. Click Share

To revoke access, open the share dialog and click Revoke access next to the user's name.

docs.title: Shared Session Restrictions
docs.text:
• Sessions shared with you as "read-only" cannot be modified — the input area is replaced with a lock icon and message
  • Sessions received from others cannot be renamed, deleted, or re-shared
  • When someone shares a session with you, a blue notification banner appears at the top of your chat

docs.title: Export Formats
docs.text: Format Extension Description Markdown .md Human-readable, includes images JSON .json Machine-readable, full data HTML .html Standalone web page TXT .txt Plain text PDF .pdf Formatted document with embedded images

docs.title: Export Steps
docs.text:
1. Open the session you want to export
  2. Click the Export button at the top of the chat
  3. Select the format (PDF, Markdown, etc.)
  4. Download the file

Note

Export lives in the chat view. The Sessions page itself offers create, rename, delete, share and add-to-project actions on session cards, but no export controls.

docs.title: Organizing Sessions into Projects
docs.text: Use Add to project on a session card to link it to a project alongside related reports, plots and datasets.

docs.title: Search Sessions
docs.text:
Search across all sessions:

  1. Navigate to Search in the sidebar
  2. Enter search query
  3. Optionally filter by session or date range
  4. Click on a result to navigate to that conversation

docs.title: Automatic Behavior
docs.text:
• A default session is created automatically
  • Sessions are saved to PostgreSQL
  • Messages include timestamps
  • Images are stored as BLOBs with file references

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Create topic-specific sessions: Separate sessions for different analyses
  2. Use descriptive names: Name sessions after the analysis topic
  3. Export important sessions: Save valuable conversations
  4. Clean up periodically: Delete old, unneeded sessions
  5. Share for collaboration: Use sharing to work with colleagues on analyses
